            <command-message>plan</command-message>
            <command-args>je voudrais travailler sur une nouvelle fonctionnalité : setup. L'idée est de pouvoir assister un utilisateur pour configurer un context. Il lance dk setup et une serie de question le dirige pour constituer son fichier de configuration. La première question serait le nom du contexte. S'il existe déjà il faut le prévenir qu'il sera supprimé (oui/non). Ensuite lui proposer les différentes options importante, forge, moteur de conteneurisation, etc. Il faut identifier les questions à poser.</command-args>

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- entire: Drive the Entire CLI (entire) for checkpoints, agent sessions, code provenance, and multi-agent review. Use when the user mentions Entire, checkpoints, session tracking, "entire why/blame/experts", agent activity recaps, or when a repo contains .entire/ and you need to inspect or manage tracked agent work.
- golang-patterns: Idiomatic Go patterns, best practices, and conventions for building robust, efficient, and maintainable Go applications. Use when writing or reviewing Go code and idiomatic structure or conventions are in question.
- golang-testing: Go testing patterns including table-driven tests, subtests, benchmarks, fuzzing, and test coverage. Follows TDD methodology with idiomatic Go practices. Use when writing Go tests — table-driven cases, subtests, benchmarks, fuzzing, or coverage.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

In the devdesk Go repo (TUI app, Bubble Tea), I need to understand the configuration system to plan a new `dk setup` wizard command that interactively creates/overwrites a named "context" config file.

Please investigate and report back (concise, with file paths and line numbers):
1. `internal/config/config.go` — the full `Config` struct schema (all fields, nested structs like `App`, forge settings, network/docker settings, scan settings, etc.), and what fields have a closed set of valid values (look for functions like `ContainerEngines()`, `config.EngineAuto` etc., theme lists, secret backend options).
2. How contexts are stored on disk: where context YAML files live (look for `~/.devdesk/`, context file naming, `internal/config` functions like `Load`, `Save`, `List contexts`, `Switch context`, path resolution, default context).
3. `applyDefaults` function in config.go — what defaults get applied.
4. Any existing CLI flag/arg parsing in `main.go` (does it use `flag`, `cobra`, or something custom? how are subcommands like potential `dk setup` currently dispatched, if any exist already, e.g. `dk version`, `dk --help`).
5. Any existing "wizard" or interactive prompt patterns elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. bubbletea forms used outside the TUI, or a survey/prompt library in go.mod).
6. The forge config section — what are the two backends (gitlab, github?) and what fields does each need (mentioned in forge.md doc)? Check `docs/architecture/forge.md` and `internal/config` for forge-related struct fields.
7. Secret backend options (`app.secret_backend`: auto, keyring, git-credential) — where declared.
8. Migration handling (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`) mentioned in CLAUDE.md — is there existing migration code style to mimic for a "create config from scratch" flow.

Report concisely: struct definitions (trimmed to relevant fields), function signatures with file:line, and any closed-value-set helper functions with their exact names. This is read-only research — do not write any code.

1. Read `main.go` fully — how does the binary currently parse `os.Args` / subcommands / flags? Is there already a pattern like `if len(os.Args) > 1 { switch os.Args[1] { case "version": ... } }`? What would be the natural place to add a `setup` subcommand?
2. `internal/forge` package — read `docs/architecture/forge.md` and the forge package's config-related types. What are the two backends (I believe gitlab.com/self-hosted GitLab and GitHub)? What fields does each need to be configured (URL, token, group/org, etc.)? Is there a `forge.Vocabulary` type — what does it expose (labels for "project" vs "repository" etc.)?
3. `internal/config` package — look for a `Forge` struct (fields like Type, URL, Token, DefaultGroup etc.), a `Network`/`Docker` struct, and a top-level `Context` or `Config` struct that ties them together with `App` struct (Theme, ContainerEngine, SecretBackend, etc.).
4. `internal/credentials` package — the `Storage` interface and `Select(context, preference string)` function signature — how does something obtain a storage backend to save a token during setup?
5. Look at `internal/config/engine.go` fully for `ContainerEngines()` and related constants (EngineAuto, EngineDocker, EnginePodman).
6. Check for any existing YAML marshalling helpers for writing a full context file to `~/.devdesk/contexts/<name>.yaml` or similar — the exact path template function.
7. Is there an existing "list contexts" or "does context exist" helper function I could reuse to check for a name collision (needed for the "context already exists, overwrite? yes/no" step)?

Report structs trimmed to relevant fields, and exact function signatures with file:line. This is read-only research — do not write any code or run non-readonly commands.

<result>Here is the research summary for planning the `dk setup` wizard.

## 1. `main.go` — subcommand parsing

File: `/c/Users/anthoni/projects/entire/anthnel/devdesk/main.go` (99 lines total, read in full).

There is **no subcommand dispatch at all** today — no `os.Args` parsing anywhere in `main.go`, and a repo-wide grep for `os.Args` outside test files/worktrees returned nothing. The comment at `main.go:22-31` is explicit about this:

```go
// main runs the TUI. There is no subcommand any more.
//
// `dk mcp` served the MCP server on stdio (§3.38) and is gone with it (§3.61):
// the server now lives in this process, over HTTP, started by the router.
```

`main.go:32-34`:
```go
func main() {
	runTUI()
}
```

So there used to be a `switch os.Args[1]` pattern (for `dk mcp`) but it was deliberately removed — the last subcommand was folded into the TUI itself. `runTUI()` (`main.go:36-99`) does: force TrueColor env fixup, `config.Load()`, `config.EnsureConfigDir()`, `tea.LogToFile`, theme load, `app.New(cfg)`, then `tea.NewProgram(...).Run()`.

**Natural place to add `dk setup`:** in `main()`, before `runTUI()` is called unconditionally — reintroducing exactly the kind of `if len(os.Args) > 1 { switch os.Args[1] { case "setup": ... } }` that was removed for `mcp`, e.g.:
```go
func main() {
	if len(os.Args) > 1 && os.Args[1] == "setup" {
		runSetupWizard()
		return
	}
	runTUI()
}
```
Note the comment at line 22 says "There is no subcommand any more" — reintroducing one is a real architectural reversal worth flagging/updating in that comment, not just bolting on a case.

## 2. `internal/forge` — backends and Vocabulary

Doc: `/c/Users/anthoni/projects/entire/anthnel/devdesk/docs/architecture/forge.md` (read in full).

Two backends, chosen by `config.ForgeGitLab` / `config.ForgeGitHub` (declared in `internal/config/forge.go:9-14`), switched at runtime by `session.Backend`:

`/c/Users/anthoni/projects/entire/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge/session/session.go:52-58`
```go
func Backend(forgeType, url, token string) (forge.Forge, error) {
	switch forgeType {
	case config.ForgeGitHub:
		return githubforge.New(url, token)
	default:
		return gitlabforge.New(url, token)
	}
}
```
An unknown type falls through to GitLab (default backend).

Config needed per backend lives in `config.ForgeConfig` (see §3 below) — `Type`, `URL`, `DefaultParentGroup`, `DefaultVisibility`, `CloneMethod`, `Pull.{ParallelJobs,IncludeArchived}`. The token is deliberately **not** in this struct — it's stored via `internal/credentials` keyed on URL (forge.md:46-50, `internal/config/config.go:181-183`).

`forge.Vocabulary` — `/c/Users/anthoni/projects/entire/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge/vocabulary.go:29-69`:
```go
type Vocabulary struct {
	Name string
	Namespace, Namespaces string
	Repository, Repositories string
	ChangeRequest, ChangeRequests string
	ChangeRequestShort string
	TokenLabel string
	TokenPlaceholder string
	TokenHelp string
	ExampleURL string
}
```
Resolved via `forge.VocabularyFor(forgeType string) Vocabulary` (`vocabulary.go:118-125`), from the **configured** type, not a live session — exactly the case a setup wizard needs (words before any session/auth exists). GitLab values: `Name:"GitLab"`, `Namespace:"Group"`, `Repository:"Project"`, `TokenLabel:"Personal Access Token"`, `TokenPlaceholder:"glpat-…"`, `ExampleURL:"https://gitlab.com"` (`vocabulary.go:76-89`). GitHub values: `Name:"GitHub"`, `Namespace:"Organization"`, `Repository:"Repository"`, `TokenPlaceholder:"ghp_… or github_pat_…"`, `ExampleURL:"https://github.com"` (`vocabulary.go:91-104`). Useful for driving wizard prompts/labels without hardcoding forge-specific strings.

## 3. `internal/config` — Forge/Network/App/Config structs

All in `/c/Users/anthoni/projects/entire/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config/config.go`.

```go
// config.go:14-29
type Config struct {
	App      AppConfig
	Status   StatusConfig
	Forge    ForgeConfig
	Registry RegistryConfig
	Scan     ScanConfig
	Network  NetworkConfig
	MCP      MCPConfig
	GitLab   GitLabConfig // deprecated, migrated into Forge
}
```

```go
// config.go:184-198
type ForgeConfig struct {
	Type               string // "gitlab" or "github"; empty = gitlab
	URL                string
	DefaultParentGroup string
	DefaultVisibility  string
	CloneMethod        string
	Pull               ForgePullConfig
}
type ForgePullConfig struct {
	ParallelJobs    int
	IncludeArchived bool
}
```

```go
// config.go:135-176
type AppConfig struct {
	Theme, LogFile, DefaultView, WorkspacesDir, IDECommand, TerminalCommand string
	TerminalNewWindow bool
	ShowHiddenFiles   bool
	SecretBackend     string // "auto" | "keyring" | "git-credential"
	ContainerEngine   string // "auto" | "docker" | "podman" | explicit path
}
```

```go
// config.go:100-121
type NetworkConfig struct {
	CheckTimeout, PingCount, CertExpiryWarnDays, PortsRefreshInterval int
}
```

**Note:** there is **no separate `Docker` struct** — I grepped for it; container/registry settings live under `RegistryConfig` (`config.go:280`) and `AppConfig.ContainerEngine`; "Docker" only appears in comments. Correct your assumption accordingly — nothing named `config.Docker`.

`Default()` (`config.go:537-591`) shows the zero-config baseline (`Forge.Type: ForgeGitLab`, `Forge.DefaultVisibility:"private"`, `Forge.CloneMethod:"https"`, `App.SecretBackend:"auto"`, `App.ContainerEngine: EngineAuto`, etc.) — a good template for what the wizard should default fields to.

## 4. `internal/credentials` — `Storage` and `Select`

`/c/Users/anthoni/projects/entire/anthnel/devdesk/internal/credentials/storage.go:20-24`
```go
type Storage interface {
	Save(url, token string) error
	Load(url string) (token string, err error)
	Delete(url string) error
}
```

`/c/Users/anthoni/projects/entire/anthnel/devdesk/internal/credentials/select.go:76-98`
```go
func Select(contextName, preference string) Selection
```
Order: host keyring, then git's credential helper (if not `store`), then in-memory fallback. `preference` comes from `app.secret_backend` (`PreferenceAuto`, `PreferenceKeyring`, `PreferenceGitCredential` at `select.go:31-34`). Returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}` (`select.go:43-50`); `Selection.Persists()` (`select.go:53-55`) tells you if it survives past this run.

For the wizard: call `credentials.Select(contextName, cfg.App.SecretBackend)` to get a `Selection`, then `selection.Storage.Save(cfg.Forge.URL, token)`. `Selection.Detail` is a ready-made user-facing sentence describing where the token went — worth surfacing at the end of the wizard. There's also `session.Auth.Authenticate(ctx, forgeType, url, token)` (`internal/forge/session/session.go:62`) which opens a session **and** saves the token via an `Auth` built from `credentials.NewAuth(storage)` — likely the higher-level call the wizard should make (validates the token against the real backend before persisting) rather than calling `Storage.Save` directly.

## 5. `internal/config/engine.go` — full file

`/c/Users/anthoni/projects/entire/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config/engine.go` (25 lines, read in full):
```go
const (
	EngineAuto   = "auto"
	EngineDocker = "docker"
	EnginePodman = "podman"
)

func ContainerEngines() []string { return []string{EngineAuto, EngineDocker, EnginePodman} }
```
Comment notes `ContainerEngines()` is not the full accepted set — an explicit binary path is also honored via `internal/engine.Resolve`, just not cycled in the UI. Use `ContainerEngines()` to populate a wizard prompt/select list.

## 6. Context file path / YAML writing — correction to your assumption

There is **no `~/.devdesk/contexts/<name>.yaml`** path. Contexts live flat under `~/.devdesk/`:

`/c/Users/anthoni/projects/entire/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config/config.go:857-876`
```go
// GetContextPath returns the file path for a context
// "default" -> ~/.devdesk/config.yaml
// "dev" -> ~/.devdesk/config-dev.yaml
func GetContextPath(contextName string) (string, error)
```

Writing is done by:
```go
// config.go:810-833
func SaveContext(cfg *Config, contextName string) error
```
It validates the name, ensures `~/.devdesk` exists, `yaml.Marshal(cfg)`, writes with mode `0600`. This is exactly the function the setup wizard should call to persist the finished `*Config`.

Also relevant: `config.CreateContext(contextName string) error` (`config.go:900-923`) builds `Default()`, clears `Status.Components` and `Forge.URL`, and calls `SaveContext` — a good template for "scaffold a new context" before the wizard fills in specifics, though the wizard will likely want to build a fuller `Config` itself and call `SaveContext` directly rather than `CreateContext` (which errors if the context already exists — see §7).

## 7. Existing "list contexts" / "does it exist" helpers — reusable directly

Both already exist and are exactly what's needed for the overwrite-confirmation step:

```go
// config.go:692  (list contexts by globbing config*.yaml)
func ListContexts() ([]string, error)

// config.go:836  (name-collision check)
func ContextExists(contextName string) (bool, error)
```

`ContextExists` validates the name via `ValidateContextName` (`config.go:880-896`, pattern `^[a-z0-9-]+$` or `"default"`) then `os.Stat`s the path from `GetContextPath`. The wizard should call `config.ContextExists(name)` right after the user types a context name, and branch to a "context '<name>' already exists — overwrite?" confirm step before calling `SaveContext` (which will happily clobber an existing file — it does not itself guard against overwrite; `CreateContext` does via the `exists` check at `config.go:906-912`, but errors out instead of prompting, so the wizard needs its own confirm+overwrite logic built on `ContextExists` + `SaveContext`, not `CreateContext`).</result>

1	// Package session opens a forge session and remembers its token.
2	//
3	// It is the one place that knows both backends exist, and the only reason it is
4	// a package of its own: internal/forge must not import a backend (a domain
5	// package cannot depend on its implementations), and a backend must not import
6	// its sibling. Something above both has to choose, and this is it.
7	//
8	// The credential store is **not** forge-shaped — Storage is keyed on a URL and
9	// knows nothing else — so the loading and forgetting of a token are the same
10	// code whichever platform the context targets. Only opening a session differs,
11	// and only in which constructor it calls.
12	package session
13	
14	import (
15		"context"
16		"fmt"
17	
18		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
19		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/credentials"
20		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge"
21		githubforge "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge/github"
22		gitlabforge "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge/gitlab"
23	)
24	
25	// Auth opens sessions against a host and remembers their tokens.
26	type Auth struct {
27		storage credentials.Storage
28	}
29	
30	// NewAuth builds an Auth over a secret store. A nil store is legitimate: the
31	// session still opens, and nothing is remembered.
32	func NewAuth(storage credentials.Storage) *Auth {
33		return &Auth{storage: storage}
34	}
35	
36	// Result is a live session, plus whatever could not be saved about it.
37	type Result struct {
38		Forge forge.Forge
39		User  forge.User
40		// SaveWarning is set when the session opened but the token could not be
41		// stored. It is not an error: the session is valid, only its persistence
42		// failed, and telling the user they are not logged in would be false.
43		SaveWarning string
44	}
45	
46	// Backend builds a client for a platform, without opening a session.
47	//
48	// The default is GitLab, matching config.applyDefaults: an unknown type has
49	// already been normalised by the time a context is loaded, and falling through
50	// to the one backend that has always existed is better than returning an error
51	// nothing can act on.
52	func Backend(forgeType, url, token string) (forge.Forge, error) {
53		switch forgeType {
54		case config.ForgeGitHub:
55			return githubforge.New(url, token)
56		default:
57			return gitlabforge.New(url, token)
58		}
59	}
60	
61	// Authenticate opens a session and saves the token.
62	func (a *Auth) Authenticate(ctx context.Context, forgeType, url, token string) (*Result, error) {
63		result, err := a.AuthenticateOnly(ctx, forgeType, url, token)
64		if err != nil {
65			return nil, err
66		}
67	
68		if a.storage != nil {
69			if err := a.storage.Save(url, token); err != nil {
70				result.SaveWarning = fmt.Sprintf("The token was not saved: %v. You will have to enter it again next launch.", err)
71			}
72		}
73	
74		return result, nil
75	}
76	
77	// AuthenticateOnly opens a session and writes nothing. It is the auto-login
78	// path, whose token already comes from the store.
79	func (a *Auth) AuthenticateOnly(ctx context.Context, forgeType, url, token string) (*Result, error) {
80		backend, err := Backend(forgeType, url, token)
81		if err != nil {
82			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create client: %w", err)
83		}
84	
85		// CurrentUser is the connection test: authentication succeeded exactly when
86		// the host answers with who the token belongs to.
87		user, err := backend.CurrentUser(ctx)
88		if err != nil {
89			return nil, fmt.Errorf("authentication failed: %w", err)
90		}
91	
92		return &Result{Forge: backend, User: user}, nil
93	}
94

96	//
97	// It takes no forge type, and that is not an oversight: the store is keyed on
98	// the URL, so a context that switched platform without changing host finds the
99	// token it already had — which is right, because it is the same host asking.

# `dk setup` — guided context wizard

## Context

Creating a DevDesk context today means hand-editing `~/.devdesk/config*.yaml`
or going field-by-field through the in-TUI configuration view after the app
already knows a context exists. There is no guided path for a brand new user
(or a brand new context) to answer "which forge, which container engine,
where do I keep secrets" once, in order, and get a working config file out.
`dk setup` closes that gap: a small Bubble Tea wizard, launched from the CLI
before the main TUI ever starts, that asks a short fixed sequence of
questions and writes the resulting context via the config package's existing
`SaveContext`.

Confirmed with the user:
- **Implementation**: a small dedicated Bubble Tea program (not bare stdin
  prompts), so it looks and behaves like the rest of the app (Rule 101/132
  cycle fields, Rule 120 focus styling, Rule 128 footer messages).
- **Forge token**: validated live against the real API before being saved
  (`session.Auth.Authenticate`, which calls `CurrentUser` as the connection
  test — `internal/forge/session/session.go:52-93`), not just stored blind.
- **Scope**: minimal. Context name, forge (type/URL/namespace/visibility/
  clone method/token), container engine, secret backend, theme. Everything
  else (registry, scan, network, status, mcp) is left at `config.Default()`'s
  values — the existing configuration view already covers them for anyone
  who wants to go further.

## Reused building blocks (no new abstractions needed)

| Need | Existing function |
|---|---|
| Validate a context name | `config.ValidateContextName` (`internal/config/config.go:880`) |
| Detect a name collision | `config.ContextExists` (`config.go:836`) |
| Start from sane defaults | `config.Default()` (`config.go:537`) |
| Write the finished config | `config.SaveContext(cfg, name)` (`config.go:810`) — overwrites unconditionally, which is fine since the wizard itself gets the yes/no confirmation first |
| Make the new context active | `config.SetCurrentContext(name)` (`config.go:669`) |
| Closed-value lists for cycle fields | `config.ContainerEngines()` (`engine.go:24`), `config.ForgeTypes()` (`forge.go:18`), `theme.ListThemes()` (`internal/ui/theme/manager.go:181`) |
| Forge wording per backend | `forge.VocabularyFor(forgeType)` (`internal/forge/vocabulary.go:118`) — `Namespace`, `TokenLabel`, `TokenPlaceholder`, `ExampleURL`, etc. |
| Resolve where the token gets stored | `credentials.Select(contextName, secretBackend)` (`internal/credentials/select.go:76`) → `Selection.Storage` |
| Validate + persist the token in one call | `session.NewAuth(selection.Storage).Authenticate(ctx, forgeType, url, token)` (`internal/forge/session/session.go:32,62`) |
| Themed widgets | `theme.StyleTextInput`, `theme.KeyStyle`, `theme.IconCircleSmall`, `theme.IconChevronRight`, `components.FooterMessage` (Rule 128) |

Nothing here needs a new "overwrite" config function — `SaveContext` already
clobbers, so the wizard's own confirm step is the only guard required.

## New code

### `internal/ui/setup/` (new package)

- **`model.go`** — the `tea.Model`: a `step` enum walked forward on submit,
  backward on `Esc` (Rule 111), plus the answer fields collected so far.
  Each step is either a single `textinput.Model` (context name, forge URL,
  namespace, token — masked via `textinput.EchoPassword`) or a cycle field
  (secret backend, container engine, theme, forge type, visibility, clone
  method) per Rule 132 — `←/→` to change value, never a dropdown.
  `Update()` extracts any case over 5 lines into `handle<Step>()` per
  Rule 201/Code Editing Rule 201.
- **`steps.go`** — one `render<Step>()` per step, following Rule 120's
  focus-indicator/chevron conventions, and one `validate<Step>()` where a
  step needs it (name syntax, non-empty URL).
- **`answers.go`** — a pure `buildConfig(a answers) *config.Config` that
  starts from `config.Default()` and overwrites just the fields the wizard
  asked about. Kept pure and separate from the `tea.Model` specifically so
  it is unit-testable without driving the Bubble Tea loop.
- **`commands.go`** — the `tea.Cmd`s that do I/O (Rule 110: never mutate the
  model inside a `Cmd`):
  - `checkContextExistsCmd(name)` → `ContextExistsMsg{exists bool, err error}`
  - `validateTokenCmd(ctx, forgeType, url, token, storage)` → wraps
    `session.NewAuth(storage).Authenticate(...)`, returns
    `TokenValidatedMsg{result *session.Result, err error}`
  - `saveContextCmd(cfg, name)` → `ContextSavedMsg{err error}`
  - `setCurrentContextCmd(name)` → `CurrentContextSetMsg{err error}`
- **`wizard.go`** — `Run() error`: builds the initial model and calls
  `tea.NewProgram(New()).Run()`.

### Step sequence

1. **Context name** — text input. On submit: `checkContextExistsCmd`. If it
   exists, a confirm modal (Rule 104, default answer "No", per "safe choice
   by default for a destructive action") — "Context '<name>' already exists
   and will be overwritten. Continue?". "No" returns to the name field
   instead of aborting the whole wizard.
2. **Secret backend** — cycle field: `auto` (default) / `keyring` /
   `git-credential`.
3. **Container engine** — cycle field: `config.ContainerEngines()`
   (`auto` default / `docker` / `podman`). A literal binary path stays a
   configuration-view-only feature, consistent with the "minimal" scope.
4. **Theme** — cycle field over `theme.ListThemes()` (always at least
   `"default"`).
5. **Forge type** — cycle field: `config.ForgeTypes()` (`gitlab` default /
   `github`).
6. **Forge URL** — text input, pre-filled with
   `forge.VocabularyFor(type).ExampleURL`, editable for self-hosted GitLab.
7. **Forge namespace** — text input, optional, labeled with
   `vocabulary.Namespace` (Group/Organization).
8. **Forge visibility** — cycle field: `private` (default) / `public`, plus
   `internal` only when the forge type is `gitlab` (GitHub has no
   equivalent — mirrors the coercion already documented for the
   configuration view, `docs/architecture/configuration.md:226-229`).
9. **Forge clone method** — cycle field: `https` (default) / `ssh`.
10. **Forge token** — masked text input, optional (`Enter` on empty skips
    straight to the summary with no token stored). On non-empty submit:
    resolve `credentials.Select(name, secretBackend)`, then
    `validateTokenCmd` — footer shows a spinner (Rule 128) while it runs.
    - Success → proceed.
    - Failure → footer error (Rule 128, `Error` level) with the choice to
      retype the token or skip it (leave unset — can be entered later via
      the normal auth view).
11. **Summary** — read-only recap of every answer. `Enter` writes
    (`saveContextCmd`), `Esc` steps back one field at a time to correct
    something (consistent with the rest of the sequence — no jump-to-field).
12. **Set as current?** — confirm modal, default "Yes" —
    `setCurrentContextCmd` on accept.
13. **Done** — prints the path written and a one-line hint (`Run "dk" to
    start.`), then quits.

`Ctrl+C` quits at any step, as everywhere else in the app.

### `main.go`

Reinstate a single subcommand case — the comment block at `main.go:22-31`
currently states "There is no subcommand any more" (true since `dk mcp` was
folded into the TUI in §3.61); that comment must be updated to reflect this
deliberate, narrow exception rather than a reversal of the policy:

```go
func main() {
	if len(os.Args) > 1 && os.Args[1] == "setup" {
		if err := setup.Run(); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "setup failed:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		return
	}
	runTUI()
}
```

No generic flag-parsing framework is introduced — one literal case, matching
the minimal-footprint precedent the removed `mcp` case set.

## Verification

- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...`.
- `golangci-lint run` (Rule 301/305) — zero warnings before considering this
  done.
- Unit tests in `internal/ui/setup/`:
  - `buildConfig` against a representative `answers` value — asserts the
    resulting `*config.Config` matches expectations (pure function, no
    Bubble Tea needed).
  - `Model.Update` driven directly with `tea.KeyMsg`/custom messages (same
    pattern as `internal/app/app_test.go`) to cover: name-collision →
    overwrite-confirm → back-to-name-on-"No"; cycle-field wrapping in both
    directions; token-validation failure keeping the wizard on the token
    step with a footer error set.
- Manual run: `go run . setup` in an interactive terminal, walking the full
  happy path once against a throwaway context name, confirming the written
  YAML at `~/.devdesk/config-<name>.yaml` matches what was entered, and that
  `~/.devdesk/.current-context` is updated when accepted.
- `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` (Rule 302) before commit.

# `dk setup` — guided context wizard

## Context

Creating a DevDesk context today means hand-editing `~/.devdesk/config*.yaml`
or going field-by-field through the in-TUI configuration view after the app
already knows a context exists. There is no guided path for a brand new user
(or a brand new context) to answer "which forge, which container engine,
where do I keep secrets" once, in order, and get a working config file out.
`dk setup` closes that gap: a small Bubble Tea wizard, launched from the CLI
before the main TUI ever starts, that asks a short fixed sequence of
questions and writes the resulting context via the config package's existing
`SaveContext`.

- **Implementation**: a small dedicated Bubble Tea program (not bare stdin
  prompts), so it looks and behaves like the rest of the app (Rule 101/132

- **Forge token**: validated live against the real API before being saved

  test — `internal/forge/session/session.go:52-93`), not just stored blind.
- **Scope**: minimal. Context name, forge (type/URL/namespace/visibility/
  clone method/token), container engine, secret backend, theme. Everything
  else (registry, scan, network, status, mcp) is left at `config.Default()`'s
  values — the existing configuration view already covers them for anyone
  who wants to go further.

| Start from sane defaults | `config.Default()` (`config.go:537`) |

- **`steps.go`** — one `render<Step>()` per step, following Rule 120's
  focus-indicator/chevron conventions, and one `validate<Step>()` where a
  step needs it (name syntax, non-empty URL).
- **`answers.go`** — a pure `buildConfig(a answers) *config.Config` that
  starts from `config.Default()` and overwrites just the fields the wizard
  asked about. Kept pure and separate from the `tea.Model` specifically so
  it is unit-testable without driving the Bubble Tea loop.
- **`commands.go`** — the `tea.Cmd`s that do I/O (Rule 110: never mutate the
  model inside a `Cmd`):
  - `checkContextExistsCmd(name)` → `ContextExistsMsg{exists bool, err error}`
  - `validateTokenCmd(ctx, forgeType, url, token, storage)` → wraps
    `session.NewAuth(storage).Authenticate(...)`, returns
    `TokenValidatedMsg{result *session.Result, err error}`
  - `saveContextCmd(cfg, name)` → `ContextSavedMsg{err error}`
  - `setCurrentContextCmd(name)` → `CurrentContextSetMsg{err error}`
- **`wizard.go`** — `Run() error`: builds the initial model and calls
  `tea.NewProgram(New()).Run()`.

### Step sequence

1. **Context name** — text input. On submit: `checkContextExistsCmd`. If it
   exists, a confirm modal (Rule 104, default answer "No", per "safe choice
   by default for a destructive action") — "Context '<name>' already exists
   and will be overwritten. Continue?". "No" returns to the name field
   instead of aborting the whole wizard.
2. **Secret backend** — cycle field: `auto` (default) / `keyring` /
   `git-credential`.
3. **Container engine** — cycle field: `config.ContainerEngines()`
   (`auto` default / `docker` / `podman`). A literal binary path stays a
   configuration-view-only feature, consistent with the "minimal" scope.
4. **Theme** — cycle field over `theme.ListThemes()` (always at least
   `"default"`).
5. **Forge type** — cycle field: `config.ForgeTypes()` (`gitlab` default /
   `github`).
6. **Forge URL** — text input, pre-filled with
   `forge.VocabularyFor(type).ExampleURL`, editable for self-hosted GitLab.
7. **Forge namespace** — text input, optional, labeled with
   `vocabulary.Namespace` (Group/Organization).
8. **Forge visibility** — cycle field: `private` (default) / `public`, plus
   `internal` only when the forge type is `gitlab` (GitHub has no
   equivalent — mirrors the coercion already documented for the
   configuration view, `docs/architecture/configuration.md:226-229`).
9. **Forge clone method** — cycle field: `https` (default) / `ssh`.
10. **Forge token** — masked text input, optional (`Enter` on empty skips
    straight to the summary with no token stored). On non-empty submit:
    resolve `credentials.Select(name, secretBackend)`, then
    `validateTokenCmd` — footer shows a spinner (Rule 128) while it runs.
    - Success → proceed.
    - Failure → footer error (Rule 128, `Error` level) with the choice to
      retype the token or skip it (leave unset — can be entered later via
      the normal auth view).
11. **Summary** — read-only recap of every answer. `Enter` writes
    (`saveContextCmd`), `Esc` steps back one field at a time to correct
    something (consistent with the rest of the sequence — no jump-to-field).
12. **Set as current?** — confirm modal, default "Yes" —
    `setCurrentContextCmd` on accept.
13. **Done** — prints the path written and a one-line hint (`Run "dk" to
    start.`), then quits.

`Ctrl+C` quits at any step, as everywhere else in the app.

### `main.go`

Reinstate a single subcommand case — the comment block at `main.go:22-31`
currently states "There is no subcommand any more" (true since `dk mcp` was
folded into the TUI in §3.61); that comment must be updated to reflect this
deliberate, narrow exception rather than a reversal of the policy:

```go
func main() {
	if len(os.Args) > 1 && os.Args[1] == "setup" {
		if err := setup.Run(); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "setup failed:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		return
	}
	runTUI()
}
```

No generic flag-parsing framework is introduced — one literal case, matching
the minimal-footprint precedent the removed `mcp` case set.

## Verification

- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...`.
- `golangci-lint run` (Rule 301/305) — zero warnings before considering this
  done.
- Unit tests in `internal/ui/setup/`:
  - `buildConfig` against a representative `answers` value — asserts the
    resulting `*config.Config` matches expectations (pure function, no
    Bubble Tea needed).
  - `Model.Update` driven directly with `tea.KeyMsg`/custom messages (same
    pattern as `internal/app/app_test.go`) to cover: name-collision →
    overwrite-confirm → back-to-name-on-"No"; cycle-field wrapping in both
    directions; token-validation failure keeping the wizard on the token
    step with a footer error set.
- Manual run: `go run . setup` in an interactive terminal, walking the full
  happy path once against a throwaway context name, confirming the written
  YAML at `~/.devdesk/config-<name>.yaml` matches what was entered, and that
  `~/.devdesk/.current-context` is updated when accepted.
- `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` (Rule 302) before commit.

1	package main
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"log"
6		"os"
7	
8		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/app"
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
11		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
12	)
13	
14	func getCurrentContextName() string {
15		ctx, err := config.GetCurrentContext()
16		if err != nil || ctx == "" {
17			return "default"
18		}
19		return ctx
20	}
21	
22	// main runs the TUI. There is no subcommand any more.
23	//
24	// `dk mcp` served the MCP server on stdio (§3.38) and is gone with it (§3.61):
25	// the server now lives in this process, over HTTP, started by the router. What
26	// that deletes is the flag set, the argument dispatch, and the ordering
27	// constraint that used to sit here — everything below writes to stdout, and in
28	// stdio stdout *was* the protocol channel, so a single warning printed before
29	// the server started made the client report a JSON parse error naming nothing.
30	// Over HTTP the two do not share a channel, so the constraint is gone rather
31	// than relaxed.
32	func main() {
33		runTUI()
34	}
35	
36	func runTUI() {
37		// Force TrueColor if Windows Terminal is detected (WSL does not propagate COLORTERM)
38		if os.Getenv("WT_SESSION") != "" && os.Getenv("COLORTERM") == "" {
39			_ = os.Setenv("COLORTERM", "truecolor")
40		}
41	
42		// Load the configuration
43		cfg, err := config.Load()
44		if err != nil {
45			fmt.Printf("Error loading config: %v\n", err)
46			fmt.Println("Using default configuration.")
47			cfg = config.Default()
48		}
49	
50		// Create the config directory if it does not exist
51		if err := config.EnsureConfigDir(); err != nil {
52			fmt.Printf("Warning: Could not create config directory: %v\n", err)
53		}
54	
55		// Always enable logging to a file to avoid polluting the TUI interface
56		logFile, err := tea.LogToFile(cfg.App.LogFile, "debug")
57		if err != nil {
58			fmt.Printf("Warning: Could not create log file: %v\n", err)
59		} else {
60			defer func() { _ = logFile.Close() }()
61			log.Printf("=== DevDesk Started ===")
62			log.Printf("Config loaded from context: %s", getCurrentContextName())
63			log.Printf("Log file: %s", cfg.App.LogFile)
64			log.Printf("DEBUG mode: %v", len(os.Getenv("DEBUG")) > 0)
65		}
66	
67		// Load and apply the saved theme
68		if cfg.App.Theme != "" && cfg.App.Theme != "dark" {
69			t, err := theme.LoadTheme(cfg.App.Theme)
70			if err != nil {
71				log.Printf("Warning: Could not load theme '%s': %v, using default", cfg.App.Theme, err)
72			} else {
73				theme.ApplyTheme(t)
74				theme.CurrentThemeName = cfg.App.Theme
75				log.Printf("Theme loaded: %s", cfg.App.Theme)
76			}
77		}
78	
79		// Create the application with the router
80		m := app.New(cfg)
81	
82		// Bubble Tea program options
83		opts := []tea.ProgramOption{
84			tea.WithAltScreen(), // Full-screen mode
85		}
86	
87		// Start the Bubble Tea program
88		p := tea.NewProgram(m, opts...)
89	
90		// The router needs the handle before the loop starts: an MCP request
91		// reaches Update() through p.Send, and there is no other legal door
92		// (Rule 110). Written here, once, while nothing else is running.
93		m.AttachProgram(p)
94	
95		if _, err := p.Run(); err != nil {
96			fmt.Printf("Error running application: %v\n", err)
97			os.Exit(1)
98		}
99	}
100

1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"os"
6		"path/filepath"
7		"regexp"
8		"strings"
9	
10		"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
11	)
12	
13	// Config represents the application's complete configuration
14	type Config struct {
15		App      AppConfig      `yaml:"app"`
16		Status   StatusConfig   `yaml:"status"`
17		Forge    ForgeConfig    `yaml:"forge"`
18		Registry RegistryConfig `yaml:"registry"`
19		Scan     ScanConfig     `yaml:"scan"`
20		Network  NetworkConfig  `yaml:"network"`
21		MCP      MCPConfig      `yaml:"mcp"`
22	
23		// GitLab is what `forge:` replaced. Same treatment as Docker above, and for
24		// the same reason: a context targets one forge, so the section is named
25		// after the role rather than after the one implementation there was.
26		//
27		// Deprecated: use Forge.
28		GitLab GitLabConfig `yaml:"gitlab,omitempty"`
29	}
30	
31	// MCPConfig governs the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP (§3.61).
32	//
33	// It was a read-only stdio subcommand, `dk mcp` (§3.38). Three of that entry's
34	// decisions were reversed together: an agent running in a container cannot
35	// execute the host binary, which was §3.38's own open question 1 and became the
36	// only case anyone had.
37	//
38	// Enabled is false by default and that is the whole safety story: turning it on
39	// is the moment the user decides an agent may reach this context. Nothing
40	// migrates it, and nothing turns it on as a side effect.
41	//
42	// **What it means widened with §3.61, and nothing re-asks.** Under §3.38 it
43	// meant a read-only server on stdio, started by the client, with no listener at
44	// all; it now opens a loopback port and — `expose` being empty by default —
45	// serves the action tier as well. A context that said yes to the first is not
46	// asked again about the second, and a file written before §3.61 is recognisable
47	// (it carries no `listen`), so a narrower default was available and was
48	// deliberately not taken: the setting has always meant "an agent may reach this
49	// context", the widening is the entry's whole subject, and a migration would be
50	// ceremony around a decision its only user had just made. It is written here
51	// rather than left for someone to discover.
52	//
53	// There is no setting for the `Match` of a secret finding, and its absence is
54	// the guarantee. The entry proposed `redact_secret_matches: true` while also
55	// classing the string itself as never exposed — a setting whose other value is
56	// refused is a parameter that has to be ignored (§3.39). Worse, `false` is a
57	// bool's zero value, so every file written before the key existed would decode
58	// to "do not redact": the exact shape of D12. The tool schemas simply have
59	// nowhere to carry the string, which is the guarantee `context_get` already
60	// gets by construction (§3.9).
61	type MCPConfig struct {
62		// Enabled decides whether the TUI serves at all. The refusal names this
63		// setting and the context, because activating it in the wrong one is
64		// otherwise an hour spent looking at a server that will not start.
65		Enabled bool `yaml:"enabled"`
66	
67		// Expose is an **allow-list** of tool names; empty means every declared
68		// tool. It is not a deny-list, for the reason §3.38 gives in the other
69		// direction: a tool never registered cannot fail to be excluded, whereas a
70		// deny-list is one forgotten line away from exposing what arrives next.
71		Expose []string `yaml:"expose,omitempty"`
72	
73		// Listen is the address the server binds, and it is a loopback address
74		// because that is both the most closed bind available and the one that
75		// works: on Docker Desktop a container reaching `host.docker.internal`
76		// arrives at the host's loopback, so a sandboxed agent is served without
77		// the LAN ever being offered the port. The sandbox's own network policy is
78		// a second lock — the port has to be allowed there by name.
79		//
80		// It is a setting rather than a literal for one reason, and it is not
81		// configurability: on native Linux Docker `host.docker.internal` does not
82		// reach the host's loopback, and the bridge gateway would have to be bound
83		// instead. That case does not exist here and is not handled — but a literal
84		// would have to be rewritten, where a setting has to be documented.
85		//
86		// An empty value means the default, never "listen nowhere": the zero value
87		// of a string cannot be allowed to read as a choice, which is the shape of
88		// D12. applyDefaults fills it.
89		Listen string `yaml:"listen,omitempty"`
90	}
91	
92	// DefaultMCPListen is where the server binds when the context does not say.
93	//
94	// Loopback, and a port high enough to be out of the way. It is named rather
95	// than inlined because applyDefaults and Default both need it, and a second
96	// literal is how the two drift.
97	const DefaultMCPListen = "127.0.0.1:7777"
98	
99	// NetworkConfig holds what the netdiag view runs on.
100	type NetworkConfig struct {
101		// CheckTimeout is how long one probe waits for an answer, in seconds.
102		//
103		// One setting rather than five: netcheck held 5 s for DNS and the dial, 8 s
104		// for TLS and HTTP and 4 s for the ping, and nothing anywhere argued for the
105		// split — it read as five separate guesses. The default is the old maximum,
106		// so nothing that answers today starts failing; the cost is that an
107		// unreachable host now spends 8 s on DNS instead of 5, which the staged
108		// progress line makes legible rather than mysterious.
109		CheckTimeout int `yaml:"check_timeout"`
110	
111		// PingCount is how many ICMP echo requests one reachability probe sends.
112		PingCount int `yaml:"ping_count"`
113	
114		// CertExpiryWarnDays is how close a certificate may come to expiring before
115		// the TLS check warns. Thirty days is a renewal cycle.
116		CertExpiryWarnDays int `yaml:"cert_expiry_warn_days"`
117	
118		// PortsRefreshInterval is how often the Ports tab re-reads the socket
119		// table, in seconds.
120		PortsRefreshInterval int `yaml:"ports_refresh_interval"`
121	}
122	
123	// Network defaults. They are the values internal/netcheck and the netdiag view
124	// held as constants before they became settings, so a config that predates them
125	// behaves exactly as it did — except CheckTimeout, which is the old maximum
126	// rather than any one of the five values it replaces.
127	const (
128		DefaultCheckTimeout         = 8
129		DefaultPingCount            = 3
130		DefaultCertExpiryWarnDays   = 30
131		DefaultPortsRefreshInterval = 2
132	)
133	
134	// AppConfig holds the app's global settings
135	type AppConfig struct {
136		Theme           string `yaml:"theme"`
137		LogFile         string `yaml:"log_file"`
138		DefaultView     string `yaml:"default_view"`
139		WorkspacesDir   string `yaml:"workspaces_dir"`
140		IDECommand      string `yaml:"ide_command"`
141		TerminalCommand string `yaml:"terminal_command"` // e.g. "kitty --directory" — empty = auto-detect
142	
143		// TerminalNewWindow decides what T does: open a shell in place, suspending
144		// the TUI (false, the default), or launch a separate terminal window (true).
145		//
146		// It is a setting rather than a second key because the capability depends on
147		// the environment and not on the intent: no window can be opened under WSL,
148		// and through SSH there is none to open. A key that is inert on two setups
149		// out of three is worse than a setting that is simply off there (§3.26).
150		TerminalNewWindow bool `yaml:"terminal_new_window"`
151	
152		// ShowHiddenFiles decides whether the workspaces view lists entries whose
153		// name starts with a dot. False is the default because that is what the
154		// view has always done, so an existing config keeps its meaning and there
155		// is nothing to migrate.
156		//
157		// It governs the listing *and* the nested-repo discovery behind S, F and A:
158		// what the view shows is what those act on, and two rules for one question
159		// would let a repository be a visible row and an invisible target at once.
160		ShowHiddenFiles bool `yaml:"show_hidden_files"`
161	
162		// SecretBackend pins where secrets are stored: "auto" (default), "keyring"
163		// for the host secret manager only, or "git-credential" for git's helper.
164		// See credentials.Select for what each one resolves to.
165		SecretBackend string `yaml:"secret_backend"`
166	
167		// ContainerEngine names the engine DevDesk drives: "auto" (default, docker
168		// if it is on PATH and podman otherwise), "docker", "podman", or an
169		// explicit path to a binary. See engine.Resolve.
170		//
171		// It sits in `app` beside ide_command and terminal_command — this section
172		// already holds the external tools the application drives — and
173		// deliberately not in `network`, which carries only netcheck's dials
174		// despite once being called `docker` (§3.67).
175		ContainerEngine string `yaml:"container_engine"`
176	}
177	
178	// ForgeConfig is the code-hosting platform this context targets — exactly one,
179	// never two (§3.6).
180	//
181	// The token is not here: it lives in the host's secret manager
182	// (§3.9). A `token:` left by an earlier version is moved into the
183	// store and then removed from the file — see secrets.go.
184	type ForgeConfig struct {
185		// Type names the backend: "gitlab" or "github". It is **declared, never
186		// sniffed** — the registry `provider` field is the precedent (§3.8), and
187		// `git.acme.com` is exactly the URL that cannot be told apart.
188		//
189		// Empty means "gitlab", which is what every file written before this key
190		// existed meant.
191		Type string `yaml:"type"`
192	
193		URL                string          `yaml:"url"`
194		DefaultParentGroup string          `yaml:"default_parent_group"`
195		DefaultVisibility  string          `yaml:"default_visibility"`
196		CloneMethod        string          `yaml:"clone_method"`
197		Pull               ForgePullConfig `yaml:"pull"`
198	}
199	
200	// ForgePullConfig holds the configuration for synchronization
201	type ForgePullConfig struct {
202		ParallelJobs    int  `yaml:"parallel_jobs"`
203		IncludeArchived bool `yaml:"include_archived"`
204	}
205	
206	// GitLabConfig is the shape `gitlab:` had. It is read at load and migrated into
207	// ForgeConfig; nothing else may use it.
208	//
209	// Deprecated: use ForgeConfig.
210	type GitLabConfig struct {
211		URL                string           `yaml:"url,omitempty"`
212		DefaultParentGroup string           `yaml:"default_parent_group,omitempty"`
213		DefaultVisibility  string           `yaml:"default_visibility,omitempty"`
214		CloneMethod        string           `yaml:"clone_method,omitempty"`
215		Pull               GitLabPullConfig `yaml:"pull,omitempty"`
216	}
217	
218	// GitLabPullConfig is `gitlab.pull:`.
219	//
220	// Deprecated: use ForgePullConfig.
221	type GitLabPullConfig struct {
222		ParallelJobs    int  `yaml:"parallel_jobs,omitempty"`
223		IncludeArchived bool `yaml:"include_archived,omitempty"`
224	}
225	
226	// RegistryItem represents a single Docker/OCI registry with optional alias support.
227	// The password is NOT stored here; it is persisted via `docker login` / system credential helper.
228	type RegistryItem struct {
229		// Slug identifies the entry inside DevDesk: it is what a member points at
230		// and what the group cache is keyed on. Everything Docker-facing stays keyed
231		// on the URL, because that is what Docker itself is keyed on — which is
232		// exactly why the URL is the wrong thing to hang a parent link on, editing
233		// one would silently orphan the group's members (§3.8, decision 1).
234		// Filled in at load for a config that predates it; see registries.go.
235		Slug string `yaml:"slug"`
236		// Kind is "registry" or "group". A group fronts several registries and is
237		// pullable itself, so both kinds share this one list (§3.8, decision A).
238		Kind string `yaml:"kind,omitempty"`
239		// Parent is the slug of the group this entry belongs to. Config entries are
240		// what the user declares and normally carry none; it is discovered members,
241		// which live in the group cache, that point back at their group.
242		Parent string `yaml:"parent,omitempty"`
243		// Provider is the repository manager serving a group — nexus, harbor,
244		// artifactory, gitlab or generic. Declared rather than sniffed from the URL.
245		Provider string `yaml:"provider,omitempty"`
246		URL      string `yaml:"url"`
247		Username string `yaml:"username"`
248		Alias    string `yaml:"alias"`
249		// RepoPrefix is what goes in front of the repository name to reach this
250		// entry: `(url, repo_prefix)` is the whole address, and browse and pull both
251		// derive from it, which is what stops them meaning two different repositories
252		// (D39, §3.18).
253		//
254		// It is declared rather than sniffed, and for the same reason `provider` is:
255		// whether a repository manager answers on a path prefix, a dedicated
256		// connector port or a subdomain is a setting on that repository, and the one
257		// endpoint that would say so is the one an ordinary pull account is refused.
258		// Empty is the ordinary case — a registry reached at its own host.
259		RepoPrefix string `yaml:"repo_prefix,omitempty"`
260		// AuthMode says whether DevDesk may send stored credentials to this entry:
261		// "credentials" or "anonymous", plus "inherit" for a member that takes its
262		// group's. It is the only per-member override the credential store can
263		// represent — see registries.go.
264		AuthMode string `yaml:"auth_mode"`
265		// AuthEnabled is what auth_mode replaced. It is read once at load, migrated
266		// into AuthMode and cleared, so it disappears from the file on the next save.
267		//
268		// Deprecated: use AuthMode.
269		AuthEnabled bool `yaml:"auth_enabled,omitempty"`
270		// ManagementURL is optional. Set it when the Docker registry URL differs from the
271		// URL used by the repository manager's API (e.g. Nexus connector subdomains,
272		// Artifactory virtual repos). The group member discovery uses this URL instead of
273		// the registry URL. Example: "https://nexus.example.com/repository/docker-group".
274		ManagementURL string `yaml:"management_url,omitempty"`
275	}
276	
277	// RegistryConfig holds the OCI registry configuration
278	//

288	// Tool source preferences. They say where a scanner is run from, which used to
289	// be decided for the user: detection resolved the binary first and only reached
290	// for Docker in the else, so a binary on PATH always won (D27).

292		// ToolSourceAuto keeps the historical resolution: the binary when there is

373	// Load loads the configuration from the current context
374	func Load() (*Config, error) {
375		ctx, err := GetCurrentContext()
376		if err != nil {
377			// Fallback to default on error
378			ctx = "default"
379		}
380	
381		cfg, err := LoadContext(ctx)
382		if err != nil {
383			// If the file does not exist, return the default config
384			if os.IsNotExist(err) || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "does not exist") {
385				return Default(), nil
386			}
387			// Otherwise (parsing error, permission error, etc.), propagate the error
388			return nil, err
389		}
390	
391		return cfg, nil
392	}

394	// applyDefaults applies the default values to a configuration.
395	// Returns an error when the file cannot be normalized — today
396	// only for registries (duplicate slug, missing parent group).
397	func applyDefaults(cfg *Config) error {
398		homeDir, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
399	
400		// `gitlab:` → `forge:`, and it runs **first**. That is not tidiness: every
401		// default below writes into cfg.Forge, so a migration placed after them
402		// would find a block that is no longer empty and take the field-by-field
403		// path — where every field is already filled with a default, and the user's
404		// own `parallel_jobs: 7` is silently dropped. Measured, not theorised: it
405		// is what the first draft did, and the retired-keys test caught it.
406		//
407		// The other half of the reason is `docker:` → `network:`'s: yaml.Unmarshal
408		// is not strict here, so an un-migrated block is dropped in silence, and the
409		// silence would point a context at no host at all.
410		migrateGitLabSection(cfg)
411	
412		// "dark" was a third name for the built-in theme: LoadTheme accepts "",
413		// "dark" and "default" alike, but ListThemes only ever offers "default", so
414		// a config saying "dark" named a theme no picker could show. Normalised at
415		// load; LoadTheme still accepts the old name for a file not yet rewritten.
416		if cfg.App.Theme == "" || cfg.App.Theme == "dark" {
417			cfg.App.Theme = "default"
418		}
419		if cfg.App.LogFile == "" {
420			cfg.App.LogFile = filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk", "devdesk.log")
421		}
422		if cfg.App.DefaultView == "" {
423			cfg.App.DefaultView = "dashboard"
424		}
425		if cfg.App.WorkspacesDir == "" {
426			cfg.App.WorkspacesDir = filepath.Join(homeDir, "workspaces")
427		}
428		if cfg.App.IDECommand == "" {
429			cfg.App.IDECommand = "code"
430		}
431		// Left empty, credentials.Select already treats this as "auto"; naming it
432		// keeps the setting inside the closed set the configuration view cycles
433		// through, so the first arrow press does not jump somewhere arbitrary.
434		if cfg.App.SecretBackend == "" {
435			cfg.App.SecretBackend = "auto"
436		}
437		// Same reason: engine.Resolve reads "" as auto, but the configuration view
438		// cycles a closed set and a value outside it has nowhere to start from.
439		if cfg.App.ContainerEngine == "" {
440			cfg.App.ContainerEngine = EngineAuto
441		}
442		if cfg.Status.RefreshInterval == 0 {
443			cfg.Status.RefreshInterval = 10
444		}
445		if cfg.Status.Timeout == 0 {
446			cfg.Status.Timeout = 5
447		}
448		if cfg.Forge.Type == "" {
449			cfg.Forge.Type = ForgeGitLab
450		}
451		if cfg.Forge.DefaultVisibility == "" {
452			cfg.Forge.DefaultVisibility = "private"
453		}
454		if cfg.Forge.CloneMethod == "" {
455			cfg.Forge.CloneMethod = "https"
456		}
457		if cfg.Forge.Pull.ParallelJobs == 0 {
458			cfg.Forge.Pull.ParallelJobs = 4
459		}
460		if cfg.Registry.CacheDir == "" {
461			cfg.Registry.CacheDir = filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk", "cache", "templates")
462		}
463		// Migrate old single-registry config to the new Registries list
464		if cfg.Registry.URL != "" && len(cfg.Registry.Registries) == 0 {
465			cfg.Registry.Registries = []RegistryItem{{
466				URL:      cfg.Registry.URL,
467				Username: cfg.Registry.Username,
468				AuthMode: AuthCredentials,
469			}}
470		}
471		if cfg.Scan.CacheDir == "" {
472			cfg.Scan.CacheDir = filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk", "cache", "scans")
473		}
474		if cfg.Scan.MaxCachedReports == 0 {
475			cfg.Scan.MaxCachedReports = 50
476		}
477		if cfg.Scan.Timeout == 0 {
478			cfg.Scan.Timeout = 300
479		}
480		if cfg.Scan.MaxConcurrentScans == 0 {
481			cfg.Scan.MaxConcurrentScans = 3
482		}
483		// An address the file does not carry is the default, never "nowhere":
484		// a bind that silently does not happen would look exactly like a server
485		// that is off, and `mcp.enabled` is what answers that question.
486		if cfg.MCP.Listen == "" {
487			cfg.MCP.Listen = DefaultMCPListen
488		}
489	
490		// Auto is the historical resolution, so a config that predates the setting
491		// keeps behaving exactly as it did.
492		if cfg.Scan.TrivySource == "" {
493			cfg.Scan.TrivySource = ToolSourceAuto
494		}
495		if cfg.Scan.GitleaksSource == "" {
496			cfg.Scan.GitleaksSource = ToolSourceAuto
497		}
498		if cfg.Scan.PlumberSource == "" {
499			cfg.Scan.PlumberSource = ToolSourceAuto
500		}
501	
502		if cfg.Network.CheckTimeout == 0 {
503			cfg.Network.CheckTimeout = DefaultCheckTimeout
504		}
505		if cfg.Network.PingCount == 0 {
506			cfg.Network.PingCount = DefaultPingCount
507		}
508		if cfg.Network.CertExpiryWarnDays == 0 {
509			cfg.Network.CertExpiryWarnDays = DefaultCertExpiryWarnDays
510		}
511		if cfg.Network.PortsRefreshInterval == 0 {
512			cfg.Network.PortsRefreshInterval = DefaultPortsRefreshInterval
513		}
514	
515		// Backward compat: configs created before the scan-option booleans were introduced
516		// will have all of them at Go's zero value (false). Treat "all disabled" as
517		// "never configured" and apply sensible defaults so scans work out of the box.
518		//
519		// EnableCIScore is read here but never written below, and the asymmetry is
520		// the point. It is newer than the four, so a file that predates them has it
521		// false too and the migration still fires; but "the four off and CI on" is a
522		// deliberate configuration — the user asked for CI alone — and forcing vuln
523		// and secret back on would overwrite it on every load. Leaving it out of the
524		// condition is what a test caught.
525		if !cfg.Scan.EnableVuln && !cfg.Scan.EnableSecret && !cfg.Scan.EnableMisconfig &&
526			!cfg.Scan.EnableLicense && !cfg.Scan.EnableCIScore {
527			cfg.Scan.EnableVuln = true
528			cfg.Scan.EnableSecret = true
529		}
530	
531		// Last, so that the registry migrated from the legacy single-registry keys
532		// above gets a slug like every other one.
533		return normalizeRegistries(cfg.Registry.Registries)
534	}

689	// ListContexts discovers the available contexts by listing config-*.yaml files
690	// Returns a slice of context names (without the "config-" prefix or ".yaml" suffix)
691	// Always includes "default" if config.yaml exists
692	func ListContexts() ([]string, error) {
693		homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()
694		if err != nil {
695			return nil, err
696		}
697	
698		configDir := filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk")
699		contexts := []string{}
700	
701		// Check the default context
702		defaultPath := filepath.Join(configDir, "config.yaml")
703		if _, err := os.Stat(defaultPath); err == nil {
704			contexts = append(contexts, "default")
705		}
706	
707		// Glob for named contexts
708		pattern := filepath.Join(configDir, "config-*.yaml")
709		matches, err := filepath.Glob(pattern)
710		if err != nil {
711			return nil, err
712		}
713	
714		for _, match := range matches {
715			// Extract the name: config-{name}.yaml -> {name}
716			basename := filepath.Base(match)
717			name := strings.TrimPrefix(basename, "config-")
718			name = strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".yaml")
719			contexts = append(contexts, name)
720		}
721	
722		return contexts, nil
723	}

725	// LoadContext loads the configuration for a specific context
726	// contextName = "default" -> config.yaml
727	// contextName = "dev" -> config-dev.yaml
728	func LoadContext(contextName string) (*Config, error) {
729		if err := ValidateContextName(contextName); err != nil {
730			return nil, err
731		}
732	
733		configPath, err := GetContextPath(contextName)
734		if err != nil {
735			return nil, err
736		}
737	
738		// Check whether the file exists
739		if _, err := os.Stat(configPath); os.IsNotExist(err) {
740			return nil, fmt.Errorf("context '%s' does not exist (no file at %s)", contextName, configPath)
741		}
742	
743		// Read and parse YAML
744		data, err := os.ReadFile(configPath)
745		if err != nil {
746			return nil, err
747		}
748	
749		var cfg Config
750		if err := yaml.Unmarshal(data, &cfg); err != nil {
751			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse context '%s': %w", contextName, err)
752		}
753	
754		// Apply the default values
755		if err := applyDefaults(&cfg); err != nil {
756			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid context '%s': %w", contextName, err)
757		}
758	
759		// Expand paths (tildes)
760		if home, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil {
761			cfg.ExpandPaths(home)
762		}
763	
764		return &cfg, nil
765	}

767	// ExpandPaths expands tildes (~) in configuration paths
768	func (c *Config) ExpandPaths(homeDir string) {
769		expand := func(path string) string {
770			if strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") {
771				return filepath.Join(homeDir, path[2:])
772			}
773			return path
774		}
775	
776		c.App.LogFile = expand(c.App.LogFile)
777		c.App.WorkspacesDir = expand(c.App.WorkspacesDir)
778		c.Registry.CacheDir = expand(c.Registry.CacheDir)
779		c.Scan.CacheDir = expand(c.Scan.CacheDir)
780		c.Scan.TrivyPath = expand(c.Scan.TrivyPath)
781		c.Scan.GitleaksPath = expand(c.Scan.GitleaksPath)
782		c.Scan.GitleaksConfig = absolute(expand(c.Scan.GitleaksConfig))
783		c.Scan.PlumberConfig = absolute(expand(c.Scan.PlumberConfig))
784	}
785	
786	// absolute pins a configured file path to one meaning.
787	//
788	// A relative gitleaks_config does not mean the same thing on both sides of the
789	// Docker boundary — DevDesk's working directory in binary mode, the container's
790	// in Docker mode — and the file is now mounted, so the two readings would
791	// disagree about which file is scanned with. Resolving it here settles it
792	// against DevDesk's own working directory, once, at load: the path that gets
793	// mounted and the path the configuration view shows are then the same string.
794	//
795	// A path that cannot be resolved is left as it was rather than dropped:
796	// RunGitleaks refuses an unreadable config with the reason, and that is a
797	// better place to fail than a config file that silently loses a setting.
798	func absolute(path string) string {
799		if path == "" {
800			return ""
801		}
802		abs, err := filepath.Abs(path)
803		if err != nil {
804			return path
805		}
806		return abs
807	}

809	// SaveContext saves the configuration to a specific context file
810	func SaveContext(cfg *Config, contextName string) error {
811		if err := ValidateContextName(contextName); err != nil {
812			return err
813		}
814	
815		configPath, err := GetContextPath(contextName)
816		if err != nil {
817			return err
818		}
819	
820		// Ensure the directory exists
821		if err := EnsureConfigDir(); err != nil {
822			return err
823		}
824	
825		// Marshal to YAML
826		data, err := yaml.Marshal(cfg)
827		if err != nil {
828			return err
829		}
830	
831		// Write the file
832		return os.WriteFile(configPath, data, 0600)
833	}

858	// "default" -> ~/.devdesk/config.yaml

860	func GetContextPath(contextName string) (string, error) {
861		homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()
862		if err != nil {
863			return "", err
864		}
865	
866		configDir := filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk")
867	
868		var filename string
869		if contextName == "default" {
870			filename = "config.yaml"

878	// ValidateContextName validates the format of the context name
879	// Must be "default" or match ^[a-z0-9-]+$
880	func ValidateContextName(name string) error {
881		if name == "default" {
882			return nil
883		}
884	
885		// Pattern: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens
886		matched, err := regexp.MatchString("^[a-z0-9-]+$", name)
887		if err != nil {
888			return err
889		}
890	
891		if !matched {
892			return fmt.Errorf("invalid context name '%s': must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens", name)
893		}

895		return nil
