1	package components
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge"
6		"strings"
7	
8		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
9		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
10		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
11	
12		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
13	)
14	
15	// descWrapWidth is the number of runes per visual line for the description field.
16	const descWrapWidth = 80
17	
18	// FormType represents the type of creation form
19	type FormType int
20	
21	const (
22		FormTypeGroup FormType = iota
23		FormTypeProject
24	)
25	
26	// resourceTypeLabels are what the two kinds are called, in cycle order. They
27	// come from the forge's vocabulary rather than being written here: a GitLab
28	// user creates a Group or a Project, a GitHub user an Organization or a
29	// Repository, and this component knows neither (§3.6).
30	func resourceTypeLabels(v forge.Vocabulary) [2]string {
31		return [2]string{v.Namespace, v.Repository}
32	}
33	
34	// CreationForm is a form for creating GitLab groups or projects
35	type CreationForm struct {
36		resourceType   int       // 0=namespace, 1=repository
37		resourceLabels [2]string // the forge's words for the two, in cycle order
38		formType       FormType  // kept in sync with resourceType
39		parentName     string    // Name of parent group (for display)
40		// parentID is the forge's opaque identifier for the parent namespace, empty
41		// at the root. It was an int64 — GitLab's numeric id — which is exactly what
42		// §3.6 made opaque: the form carries it and never reads it.
43		parentID        string
44		nameInput       textinput.Model
45		descInput       WrappedInput
46		visibility      int      // 0=private, 1=internal, 2=public
47		visibilities    []string // visibility options
48		templates       []string // for projects: available templates
49		templateIdx     int      // selected template index
50		templateScroll  int      // scroll offset for template dropdown
51		templateWarning string   // warning message if template loading failed
52		// focusedField: 0=resourceType, 1=name, 2=desc, 3=visibility, 4=template (project only), 4or5=submit
53		focusedField int
54		width        int
55		height       int
56		err          string
57	}
58	
59	// CreationFormSubmitMsg is sent when form is submitted
60	type CreationFormSubmitMsg struct {
61		FormType    FormType
62		Name        string
63		Description string
64		Visibility  string
65		Template    string // for projects
66		ParentID    string
67	}
68	
69	// CreationFormCancelMsg is sent when form is cancelled
70	type CreationFormCancelMsg struct{}
71	
72	// Description character limit (GitLab limit is 250)
73	const descriptionCharLimit = 250
74	
75	// maxVisibleTemplates is the maximum number of templates visible in the dropdown
76	const maxVisibleTemplates = 7
77	
78	// formTypeFromResourceType converts a resource type index to FormType.
79	func formTypeFromResourceType(rt int) FormType {
80		if rt == 1 {
81			return FormTypeProject
82		}
83		return FormTypeGroup
84	}
85	
86	// NewCreationForm creates the unified group/project creation form.
87	// defaultResourceType: 0=Group, 1=Project.
88	// focusedField starts at 0 (Type) so the user can immediately cycle the resource type.
89	func NewCreationForm(defaultResourceType int, parentName string, parentID string, defaultVisibility string, templates []string, v forge.Vocabulary) *CreationForm {
90		nameInput := textinput.New()
91		nameInput.Placeholder = "name"
92		nameInput.CharLimit = 100
93		nameInput.Width = 50
94		theme.StyleTextInput(&nameInput)
95	
96		descInput := NewWrappedInput(descWrapWidth, descriptionCharLimit, "description (optional)")
97	
98		visibilities := []string{"private", "internal", "public"}
99		visIdx := 0
100		for i, v := range visibilities {
101			if v == defaultVisibility {
102				visIdx = i
103				break
104			}
105		}
106	
107		// Add "none" template option at the beginning
108		allTemplates := append([]string{"none"}, templates...)
109	
110		return &CreationForm{
111			resourceType:   defaultResourceType,
112			resourceLabels: resourceTypeLabels(v),
113			formType:       formTypeFromResourceType(defaultResourceType),
114			parentName:     parentName,
115			parentID:       parentID,
116			nameInput:      nameInput,
117			descInput:      descInput,
118			visibility:     visIdx,
119			visibilities:   visibilities,
120			templates:      allTemplates,
121			templateIdx:    0,
122			focusedField:   0, // start on Type
123		}
124	}
125	
126	// SetTemplateWarning sets a warning message displayed near the template field
127	func (f *CreationForm) SetTemplateWarning(msg string) {
128		f.templateWarning = msg
129	}
130	
131	// Update handles messages
132	func (f *CreationForm) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*CreationForm, tea.Cmd) {
133		switch msg := msg.(type) {
134		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
135			f.width = msg.Width
136			f.height = msg.Height
137			f.descInput.SetDisplayWidth(msg.Width)
138	
139		case tea.KeyMsg:
140			return f.handleKeyMsg(msg)
141		}
142	
143		// Update focused text input
144		var cmd tea.Cmd
145		switch f.focusedField {
146		case 1:
147			f.nameInput, cmd = f.nameInput.Update(msg)
148		case 2:
149			f.descInput, cmd = f.descInput.Update(msg)
150		}
151	
152		return f, cmd
153	}
154	
155	// maxField returns the index of the submit button (last field).
156	func (f *CreationForm) maxField() int {
157		if f.resourceType == 1 && len(f.templates) > 0 {
158			return 5
159		}
160		return 4
161	}
162	
163	func (f *CreationForm) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (*CreationForm, tea.Cmd) {
164		max := f.maxField()
165	
166		switch msg.String() {
167		case "esc":
168			return f, func() tea.Msg { return CreationFormCancelMsg{} }
169	
170		case "down":
171			if f.isOnTemplateField() && f.templateIdx < len(f.templates)-1 {
172				f.templateDown()
173				return f, nil
174			}
175			f.focusedField = (f.focusedField + 1) % (max + 1)
176			f.updateFocus()
177			return f, nil
178	
179		case "up":
180			if f.isOnTemplateField() && f.templateIdx > 0 {
181				f.templateUp()
182				return f, nil
183			}
184			f.focusedField = (f.focusedField - 1 + max + 1) % (max + 1)
185			f.updateFocus()
186			return f, nil
187	
188		case "enter":
189			if f.focusedField == max { // Submit button
190				return f.submit()
191			}
192			// On other fields, move to next
193			f.focusedField = (f.focusedField + 1) % (max + 1)
194			f.updateFocus()
195			return f, nil
196	
197		case "left", "right":
198			// Field 0: cycle resource type (Group ↔ Project)
199			if f.focusedField == 0 {
200				if msg.String() == "left" {
201					f.resourceType = (f.resourceType - 1 + len(f.resourceLabels)) % len(f.resourceLabels)
202				} else {
203					f.resourceType = (f.resourceType + 1) % len(f.resourceLabels)
204				}
205				f.formType = formTypeFromResourceType(f.resourceType)
206				// No focus clamp here: this branch is only reached with
207				// focusedField == 0, and maxField() never drops below 4.
208				return f, nil
209			}
210			// Field 3: cycle visibility
211			if f.focusedField == 3 {
212				if msg.String() == "left" {
213					f.visibility = (f.visibility - 1 + len(f.visibilities)) % len(f.visibilities)
214				} else {
215					f.visibility = (f.visibility + 1) % len(f.visibilities)
216				}
217			}
218			return f, nil
219		}
220	
221		// Update text inputs
222		var cmd tea.Cmd
223		switch f.focusedField {
224		case 1:
225			f.nameInput, cmd = f.nameInput.Update(msg)
226		case 2:
227			f.descInput, cmd = f.descInput.Update(msg)
228		}
229	
230		return f, cmd
231	}
232	
233	// isOnTemplateField returns true if the template dropdown has focus
234	func (f *CreationForm) isOnTemplateField() bool {
235		return f.focusedField == 4 && f.resourceType == 1 && len(f.templates) > 0
236	}
237	
238	// templateDown moves template selection down by one
239	func (f *CreationForm) templateDown() {
240		if f.templateIdx < len(f.templates)-1 {
241			f.templateIdx++
242			f.adjustTemplateScroll()
243		}
244	}
245	
246	// templateUp moves template selection up by one
247	func (f *CreationForm) templateUp() {
248		if f.templateIdx > 0 {
249			f.templateIdx--
250			f.adjustTemplateScroll()
251		}
252	}
253	
254	// adjustTemplateScroll ensures the selected template is visible in the dropdown
255	func (f *CreationForm) adjustTemplateScroll() {
256		// Scroll down if selected is below visible area
257		if f.templateIdx >= f.templateScroll+maxVisibleTemplates {
258			f.templateScroll = f.templateIdx - maxVisibleTemplates + 1
259		}
260		// Scroll up if selected is above visible area
261		if f.templateIdx < f.templateScroll {
262			f.templateScroll = f.templateIdx
263		}
264	}
265	
266	func (f *CreationForm) updateFocus() {
267		f.nameInput.Blur()
268		f.descInput.Blur()
269	
270		switch f.focusedField {
271		case 1:
272			f.nameInput.Focus()
273		case 2:
274			f.descInput.Focus()
275		}
276	}
277	
278	// GetTitle returns the form title for use in the viewport breadcrumb.
279	// Includes the parent name when applicable: "New Project (parent: group/sub)".
280	func (f *CreationForm) GetTitle() string {
281		base := "New " + f.resourceLabels[f.resourceType]
282		if f.parentName != "" {
283			parent := lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(theme.ColorSecondary).Background(theme.ColorBackground).Render("(parent: " + f.parentName + ")")
284			return base + " " + parent
285		}
286		return base
287	}
288	
289	// InEditMode returns true when the form is being edited (for preventing command mode)
290	func (f *CreationForm) InEditMode() bool {
291		return true
292	}
293	
294	func (f *CreationForm) submit() (*CreationForm, tea.Cmd) {
295		name := strings.TrimSpace(f.nameInput.Value())
296		if name == "" {
297			f.err = "Name is required"
298			return f, nil
299		}
300	
301		template := ""
302		if f.formType == FormTypeProject && len(f.templates) > 0 && f.templateIdx > 0 {
303			template = f.templates[f.templateIdx]
304		}
305	
306		return f, func() tea.Msg {
307			return CreationFormSubmitMsg{
308				FormType:    f.formType,
309				Name:        name,
310				Description: strings.TrimSpace(f.descInput.Value()),
311				Visibility:  f.visibilities[f.visibility],
312				Template:    template,
313				ParentID:    f.parentID,
314			}
315		}
316	}
317	
318	// View renders the form
319	func (f *CreationForm) View() string {
320		var b strings.Builder
321	
322		b.WriteString(theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n")
323	
324		// Error message
325		if f.err != "" {
326			b.WriteString(lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorError).Render("Error: "+f.err) + "\n\n")
327		}
328	
329		// Resource type selector (cycle ←→)
330		b.WriteString(f.renderResourceTypeField())
331		b.WriteString("\n\n")
332	
333		// Name field
334		b.WriteString(f.renderField("Name", f.nameInput.View(), 1))
335		b.WriteString("\n\n")
336	
337		// Description field (multiline)
338		b.WriteString(f.renderDescriptionField())
339		b.WriteString("\n\n")
340	
341		// Visibility selector
342		b.WriteString(f.renderVisibilityField())
343		b.WriteString("\n\n")
344	
345		// Template dropdown (for projects only)
346		if f.resourceType == 1 && len(f.templates) > 0 {
347			b.WriteString(f.renderTemplateList())
348			b.WriteString("\n\n")
349		}
350	
351		// Submit button
352		b.WriteString("\n")
353		b.WriteString("  " + theme.RenderButton("Create", f.focusedField == f.maxField(), "primary"))
354		b.WriteString("\n\n")
355	
356		// Help is shown in header shortcuts
357	
358		// Return without modal border (Rule 112: forms in viewport)
359		return b.String()
360	}
361	
362	func (f *CreationForm) renderField(label, value string, fieldIdx int) string {
363		var labelStr string
364		if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
365			labelStr = theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " " + label + " " + theme.IconChevronRight)
366		} else {
367			labelStr = theme.Bg("  " + label + " " + theme.IconChevronRight)
368		}
369		return labelStr + "\n" + theme.Bg("  ") + value
370	}
371	
372	// renderResourceTypeField renders the resource type cycle selector (Rule 132).
373	func (f *CreationForm) renderResourceTypeField() string {
374		label := "Type " + theme.IconSelect + " "
375		value := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).
376			Render(f.resourceLabels[f.resourceType])
377		if f.focusedField == 0 {
378			return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+label+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
379		}
380		return theme.Bg("  "+label+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
381	}
382	
383	func (f *CreationForm) renderDescriptionField() string {
384		charCount := len([]rune(f.descInput.Value()))
385		countStyle := theme.DimStyle
386		if charCount > descriptionCharLimit-20 {
387			countStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight)
388		}
389		if charCount >= descriptionCharLimit {
390			countStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorError)
391		}
392		countStr := countStyle.Render(fmt.Sprintf(" (%d/%d)", charCount, descriptionCharLimit))
393	
394		var labelStr string
395		if f.focusedField == 2 {
396			labelStr = theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Description " + theme.IconChevronRight)
397		} else {
398			labelStr = theme.Bg("  Description " + theme.IconChevronRight)
399		}
400	
401		return labelStr + countStr + "\n" + f.descInput.View()
402	}
403	
404	// renderVisibilityField renders the visibility selector in the same single-line format as
405	// the "Target Type" field in the security view (Rule 115).
406	func (f *CreationForm) renderVisibilityField() string {
407		label := "Visibility " + theme.IconSelect + " "
408		value := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).Render(f.visibilities[f.visibility])
409		if f.focusedField == 3 {
410			return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+label+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
411		}
412		return theme.Bg("  "+label+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
413	}
414	
415	// renderTemplateList renders a vertical scrollable dropdown list for template selection
416	func (f *CreationForm) renderTemplateList() string {
417		focused := f.focusedField == 4
418	
419		var labelStr string
420		if focused {
421			labelStr = theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Template " + theme.IconSelect + " " + theme.IconChevronRight + " ")
422		} else {
423			labelStr = theme.Bg("  Template " + theme.IconSelect + " " + theme.IconChevronRight + " ")
424		}
425	
426		// Show selected template name next to label when not focused. The warning
427		// still goes out: it explains why the list is empty, and a user who never
428		// lands on this field would otherwise never learn the registry failed.
429		if !focused {
430			selected := f.templates[f.templateIdx]
431			return labelStr + theme.PrimaryColorStyle.Render(selected) + f.renderTemplateWarning()
432		}
433	
434		// Focused: render vertical dropdown list
435		var b strings.Builder
436		b.WriteString(labelStr)
437		b.WriteString("\n")
438	
439		visibleCount := maxVisibleTemplates
440		if len(f.templates) < visibleCount {
441			visibleCount = len(f.templates)
442		}
443	
444		// Scroll indicator: items above
445		if f.templateScroll > 0 {
446			b.WriteString(theme.DimStyle.Render(fmt.Sprintf("    ↑ %d more", f.templateScroll)))
447			b.WriteString("\n")
448		}
449	
450		// Render visible items
451		end := f.templateScroll + visibleCount
452		if end > len(f.templates) {
453			end = len(f.templates)
454		}
455	
456		for i := f.templateScroll; i < end; i++ {
457			tmpl := f.templates[i]
458			if i == f.templateIdx {
459				b.WriteString(theme.PrimaryColorStyle.Bold(true).Render("  " + theme.IconCircleSmall + " " + tmpl))
460			} else {
461				b.WriteString(theme.DimStyle.Render("    " + tmpl))
462			}
463			if i < end-1 {
464				b.WriteString("\n")
465			}
466		}
467	
468		// Scroll indicator: items below
469		remaining := len(f.templates) - end
470		if remaining > 0 {
471			b.WriteString("\n")
472			b.WriteString(theme.DimStyle.Render(fmt.Sprintf("    ↓ %d more", remaining)))
473		}
474	
475		b.WriteString(f.renderTemplateWarning())
476	
477		return b.String()
478	}
479	
480	// renderTemplateWarning renders the registry failure on its own line, or an
481	// empty string when the templates loaded. It is appended in both the focused
482	// and unfocused branches of renderTemplateList: the warning explains why the
483	// list is empty, so hiding it until the field takes focus tells the user
484	// nothing at the moment they need it.
485	func (f *CreationForm) renderTemplateWarning() string {
486		if f.templateWarning == "" {
487			return ""
488		}
489		return "\n" + lipgloss.NewStyle().
490			Background(theme.ColorBackground).
491			Foreground(theme.ColorError).
492			Render("    "+theme.IconWarning+" "+f.templateWarning)
493	}

1	package components
2	
3	import (
4		"sync/atomic"
5		"time"
6	
7		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
8		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
9	
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
11	)
12	
13	// FooterMessage is the one line of state every view shows below its viewport
14	// (Rules 124, 128). It owns both the text and the three-second timer, which is
15	// what makes it a component rather than a rendering helper: eight views each
16	// carried their own pair of fields, their own clear message and their own
17	// lipgloss block, and that is how the errors ended up left-aligned everywhere
18	// while the notices were centred — nobody ever centred the error branch.
19	//
20	// Usage, from Update() only (Rule 110):
21	//
22	//	case SomethingFailedMsg:
23	//	    return m, m.footer.Error("Failed to load — check logs")
24	//
25	//	default:
26	//	    if m.footer.Handle(msg) {
27	//	        return m, nil
28	//	    }
29	//
30	// And from View(), which stays read-only:
31	//
32	//	m.footer.View(width, components.Status{Text: m.actionLine()})
33	
34	// FooterMsgDuration is how long a timed message stays on screen (Rule 128).
35	//
36	// It is an exported var rather than a const because tea.Tick really sleeps, and
37	// a test that inspects a Cmd carrying this timer — testutil.Msgs runs the whole
38	// batch — pays the full three seconds per assertion. internal/ui/testutil
39	// shortens it from its init, so every view test package gets that for free; the
40	// production value is what this file states and what
41	// TestAMessageGetsThreeSeconds pins.
42	var FooterMsgDuration = 3 * time.Second
43	
44	// Level is a footer message's severity. It decides the colour and nothing else.
45	//
46	// The three are defined by what happened, not by how it feels:
47	//
48	//	LevelError   — an operation failed, or the system refused it.
49	//	LevelWarning — the action cannot be honoured as asked, but nothing failed:
50	//	               a precondition is unmet, or it is already running.
51	//	LevelInfo    — a neutral fact, or an operation that succeeded.
52	type Level int
53	
54	const (
55		LevelInfo Level = iota
56		LevelWarning
57		LevelError
58	)
59	
60	// Style returns the style a level renders in.
61	func (l Level) Style() lipgloss.Style {
62		switch l {
63		case LevelError:
64			return theme.FooterErrorStyle
65		case LevelWarning:
66			return theme.FooterWarnStyle
67		default:
68			return theme.FooterInfoStyle
69		}
70	}
71	
72	// Status is what a view derives on every frame: a progress line, a hint, or a
73	// table loading its rows. It carries no timer — a batch outlives the three
74	// seconds a message gets, which is why the sync and prune lines were rendered
75	// from state rather than assigned to footerInfo in the first place.
76	//
77	// It is a parameter of View rather than a field of FooterMessage because it is
78	// derived, not stored: containers' action line comes from BusyLabels(), which
79	// changes with no event to push it on.
80	type Status struct {
81		Text string
82		// Spinner prepends the current spinner frame — a table loading its rows.
83		Spinner bool
84		// Level colours the line, and the zero value is LevelInfo, so a status that
85		// says nothing about it renders exactly as it always did.
86		//
87		// A derived state can be a failure as legitimately as it can be progress:
88		// "Docker unreachable" is not an event that happened once, it is what is
89		// true right now, and a message would expire after three seconds — which is
90		// D47 in one field. It needs the colour of an error and the lifetime of a
91		// state, and only Status can give it both.
92		Level Level
93	}
94	
95	// footerMsgSeq numbers messages so a timer can name the one it was started for.
96	var footerMsgSeq atomic.Uint64
97	
98	// ClearFooterMsg expires the message identified by ID.
99	//
100	// The ID is what makes the type safe to share across packages. Two things would
101	// otherwise go wrong: a timer started by one view could clear the message of
102	// whichever view is active when it lands, and — the bug that was already
103	// present in all eight local implementations — a message set at t+2.9s was
104	// wiped at t+3s by its predecessor's timer.
105	type ClearFooterMsg struct{ ID uint64 }
106	
107	// PostFooterMsg puts a message in whichever footer is on screen.
108	//
109	// It exists for the router, which has none of its own: RenderFooter is the
110	// active view's (internal/app/view.go), and the one thing the router has to say
111	// — that the MCP server did not start (§3.61) — belongs on screen at startup,
112	// not in a log. Every view already offers unhandled messages to Handle, so a
113	// broadcast lands wherever the user is without any view knowing what it is
114	// about.
115	//
116	// It carries its own ID because the timer is the sender's: PostFooter builds
117	// both, so the rule that a message set without its timer never clears holds
118	// here too (Rule 128).
119	//
120	// **It lands only where a view holds a FooterMessage.** internal/ui/forge/auth
121	// renders a footer but declares none, so a broadcast posted while that view is
122	// on screen reaches nobody — and the router switches to it whenever a context
123	// has no forge credentials. That is a real gap and not a silent one: the only
124	// broadcast today is the MCP server's, and its state is also on the `mcp` tab
125	// of the configuration view, which holds it for as long as it is true rather
126	// than for three seconds. A second use of this door would need auth to declare
127	// a footer first.
128	type PostFooterMsg struct {
129		ID    uint64
130		Level Level
131		Text  string
132	}
133	
134	// PostFooter builds the broadcast and the timer that expires it.
135	//
136	// For the router. A view has its own footer and calls Info, Warn or Error on
137	// it — going through here would be a second way to do what a field already
138	// does, and the message would be adopted by whatever view is active rather than
139	// by the one that meant it.
140	func PostFooter(level Level, text string) tea.Cmd {
141		if text == "" {
142			return nil
143		}
144		id := footerMsgSeq.Add(1)
145		return tea.Batch(
146			func() tea.Msg { return PostFooterMsg{ID: id, Level: level, Text: text} },
147			tea.Tick(FooterMsgDuration, func(time.Time) tea.Msg { return ClearFooterMsg{ID: id} }),
148		)
149	}
150	
151	// FooterMessage holds the current message, its level and its identity.
152	type FooterMessage struct {
153		text         string
154		level        Level
155		id           uint64
156		spinnerFrame string
157	}
158	
159	// Info, Warn and Error set the message and return its expiry timer. Call them
160	// from Update() and return the Cmd — a message set without its timer never
161	// clears (Rule 128).
162	func (f *FooterMessage) Info(text string) tea.Cmd  { return f.set(text, LevelInfo) }
163	func (f *FooterMessage) Warn(text string) tea.Cmd  { return f.set(text, LevelWarning) }
164	func (f *FooterMessage) Error(text string) tea.Cmd { return f.set(text, LevelError) }
165	
166	func (f *FooterMessage) set(text string, level Level) tea.Cmd {
167		if text == "" {
168			f.Clear()
169			return nil
170		}
171		f.text = text
172		f.level = level
173		f.id = footerMsgSeq.Add(1)
174	
175		id := f.id
176		return tea.Tick(FooterMsgDuration, func(time.Time) tea.Msg {
177			return ClearFooterMsg{ID: id}
178		})
179	}
180	
181	// Clear removes the message now, without waiting for its timer.
182	func (f *FooterMessage) Clear() {
183		f.text = ""
184		f.level = LevelInfo
185		f.id = 0
186	}
187	
188	// Handle consumes what the component owns and reports whether it did: a
189	// ClearFooterMsg addressed to the current message, and a PostFooterMsg from the
190	// router. A stale expiry is dropped, and so is one belonging to another view:
191	// both leave the message on screen for the time it was given.
192	func (f *FooterMessage) Handle(msg tea.Msg) bool {
193		switch msg := msg.(type) {
194		case PostFooterMsg:
195			// Adopted whole, ID included: the timer that will expire it was built
196			// with that ID by the sender, and re-numbering it here would leave a
197			// message nothing ever clears.
198			f.text = msg.Text
199			f.level = msg.Level
200			f.id = msg.ID
201			return true
202	
203		case ClearFooterMsg:
204			if f.id == 0 || msg.ID != f.id {
205				return false
206			}
207			f.Clear()
208			return true
209		}
210		return false
211	}
212	
213	// SetSpinnerFrame stores the frame a loading Status renders with. Call it from
214	// the view's spinner.TickMsg handler, passing spinner.View().
215	//
216	// It takes the **rendered** spinner rather than a bare frame, which is what
217	// theme.SpinnerMessage took before it: every view already sets its spinner's
218	// Style to theme.SpinnerStyle(), so the colour is decided there and restyling
219	// here would nest one sequence inside another.
220	//
221	// That is the opposite of the rule for a table cell (Rule 122), and the
222	// difference is what is doing the measuring. A cell is measured by runewidth,
223	// which counts an escape's bytes as columns; this line is measured by
224	// lipgloss.Width, which does not.
225	func (f *FooterMessage) SetSpinnerFrame(frame string) { f.spinnerFrame = frame }
226	
227	// IsSet reports whether a message is currently displayed.
228	func (f *FooterMessage) IsSet() bool { return f.text != "" }
229	
230	// Text and Level report what is displayed. They exist for tests and for the
231	// netdiag header, which picks the active tab's message.
232	func (f *FooterMessage) Text() string { return f.text }
233	func (f *FooterMessage) Level() Level { return f.level }
234	
235	// ID identifies the message currently displayed, 0 when there is none. It is
236	// what the timer names, and it lets a test in another package build the expiry
237	// this message will receive — running the real Cmd sleeps for three seconds,
238	// which is a long time to pay per assertion.
239	func (f *FooterMessage) ID() uint64 { return f.id }
240	
241	// View renders the footer's line of text, always at the full width and always
242	// centred — including when it is empty, because Rule 124 budgets a line for it
243	// whatever it holds.
244	//
245	// Precedence: error, warning, info, then the derived status. A failure the user
246	// has not read yet matters more than the progress of what is still running.
247	func (f *FooterMessage) View(width int, status Status) string {
248		if width <= 0 {
249			return ""
250		}
251	
252		// A timed message wins over the derived status: a failure the user has not
253		// read yet matters more than the progress of what is still running.
254		//
255		// Truncation is not cosmetic — a line wider than the viewport wraps onto a
256		// second one, and the router budgeted exactly one (Rule 124). Everything
257		// below it would shift by a line.
258		if f.text != "" {
259			return centerLine(f.level.Style().Render(theme.TruncateWidth(f.text, width)), width)
260		}
261		if status.Text == "" {
262			return theme.EmptyLineBg(width)
263		}
264	
265		// lipgloss.Width, not theme.StringWidth: the frame arrives already styled,
266		// and runewidth would count its escape sequence as columns.
267		spinner, budget := "", width
268		if status.Spinner && f.spinnerFrame != "" {
269			spinner = f.spinnerFrame + theme.Bg(" ")
270			budget -= lipgloss.Width(f.spinnerFrame) + 1
271		}
272		if budget <= 0 {
273			return theme.EmptyLineBg(width)
274		}
275		return centerLine(spinner+status.Level.Style().Render(theme.TruncateWidth(status.Text, budget)), width)
276	}
277	
278	// centerLine centres already-styled content on a line filled with the app
279	// background. lipgloss does not inherit a background (Rule 115), so the padding
280	// either side has to carry one of its own.
281	func centerLine(content string, width int) string {
282		return lipgloss.NewStyle().
283			Background(theme.ColorBackground).
284			Width(width).
285			Align(lipgloss.Center).
286			Render(content)
287	}

1	package components
2	
3	import (
4		"strings"
5	
6		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
7		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
10	)
11	
12	// OptionConfirmModal is a confirmation carrying a checkbox: "do it, and do
13	// it this particular way".
14	//
15	// It used to serve deletion alone, hence its former name. §3.26 gives it a
16	// second use — purging the cache before a full scan — and it's the same
17	// need: two actions distinguished only by a modifier, with nothing in the
18	// form saying which one was destructive. Here the destructive variant is a
19	// deliberate gesture, under the eyes of whoever triggers it.
20	type OptionConfirmModal struct {
21		title   string
22		message string
23		focused int // 0 = checkbox, 1 = Yes, 2 = No
24		// option is the checkbox, and its meaning belongs to the caller:
25		// immediate deletion here, cache purge there.
26		option        bool
27		optionLabel   string
28		optionWarning string // shown when the box is checked; empty = nothing to say
29		locked        bool   // If true, the checkbox is neither editable nor focusable
30		hidden        bool   // If true, the checkbox isn't even rendered: the option has no meaning here
31		width         int
32		height        int
33	}
34	
35	// immediateDeletionLabel is the deletion option, and the reason this modal
36	// exists.
37	const (
38		immediateDeletionLabel   = "Immediate deletion (no grace period)"
39		immediateDeletionWarning = "This action is irreversible!"
40	)
41	
42	// NewOptionConfirmModal creates a confirmation with a named checkbox.
43	// No warning: an option that isn't destructive doesn't deserve one.
44	func NewOptionConfirmModal(title, message, optionLabel string) *OptionConfirmModal {
45		return &OptionConfirmModal{
46			title:       title,
47			message:     message,
48			focused:     2, // Defaults to "No"
49			optionLabel: optionLabel,
50		}
51	}
52	
53	// NewDeleteConfirmModal creates a new deletion confirmation modal.
54	// offerImmediate comes from forge.Shape.PermanentDelete: on a backend that
55	// always deletes immediately (GitHub), there is no grace period to bypass,
56	// so the checkbox has nothing to signify and isn't rendered at all — not
57	// greyed out, absent, as that field of the Shape says.
58	func NewDeleteConfirmModal(title, message string, offerImmediate bool) *OptionConfirmModal {
59		m := NewOptionConfirmModal(title, message, immediateDeletionLabel)
60		if !offerImmediate {
61			m.hidden = true
62			return m
63		}
64		m.optionWarning = immediateDeletionWarning
65		return m
66	}
67	
68	// NewDeleteConfirmModalLocked creates a modal with the "immediate deletion" checkbox pre-checked and non-editable.
69	// Use it when the project is already marked for deletion — only permanent deletion is possible.
70	func NewDeleteConfirmModalLocked(title, message string) *OptionConfirmModal {
71		m := NewDeleteConfirmModal(title, message, true)
72		m.option = true
73		m.locked = true
74		return m
75	}
76	
77	// minFocus returns the first element reachable by keyboard. The checkbox is
78	// excluded when it is locked or absent: a focusable control that ignores
79	// every keystroke, or that doesn't exist, is more confusing than a control
80	// that is simply out of reach.
81	func (m *OptionConfirmModal) minFocus() int {
82		if m.locked || m.hidden {
83			return 1
84		}
85		return 0
86	}
87	
88	// OptionConfirmModalYesMsg is sent when the user confirms. Option carries
89	// the checkbox's state, whose meaning belongs to whoever opened the modal.
90	type OptionConfirmModalYesMsg struct {
91		Option bool
92	}
93	
94	// OptionConfirmModalNoMsg is sent when the user cancels
95	type OptionConfirmModalNoMsg struct{}
96	
97	// Update updates the modal
98	func (m *OptionConfirmModal) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*OptionConfirmModal, tea.Cmd) {
99		switch msg := msg.(type) {
100		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
101			m.width = msg.Width
102			m.height = msg.Height
103	
104		case tea.KeyMsg:
105			switch msg.String() {
106			// Rule 135: ↑/↓ are the only field navigation. They cycle rather than
107			// clamp, so every control stays reachable in one direction — that is
108			// what tab used to provide before it was removed.
109			case "up":
110				m.focused = m.cycleFocus(-1)
111				return m, nil
112	
113			case "down":
114				m.focused = m.cycleFocus(1)
115				return m, nil
116	
117			case "left":
118				// If on the buttons, move to Yes
119				if m.focused == 2 {
120					m.focused = 1
121				}
122				return m, nil
123	
124			case "right":
125				// If on the buttons, move to No
126				if m.focused == 1 {
127					m.focused = 2
128				}
129				return m, nil
130	
131			case " ":
132				// Toggle the checkbox if it has focus, otherwise confirm the selection
133				if m.focused == 0 {
134					m.toggleCheckbox()
135					return m, nil
136				}
137				return m.handleConfirm()
138	
139			case "enter":
140				return m.handleConfirm()
141	
142			case "y", "Y":
143				// Shortcut for Yes
144				return m, func() tea.Msg {
145					return OptionConfirmModalYesMsg{Option: m.option}
146				}
147	
148			case "n", "N", "esc":
149				// Shortcut for No
150				return m, func() tea.Msg {
151					return OptionConfirmModalNoMsg{}
152				}
153			}
154		}
155	
156		return m, nil
157	}
158	
159	// cycleFocus rotates focus in the given direction, skipping the elements
160	// excluded by minFocus().
161	func (m *OptionConfirmModal) cycleFocus(step int) int {
162		min := m.minFocus()
163		span := 3 - min
164		return min + ((m.focused-min+step)%span+span)%span
165	}
166	
167	// toggleCheckbox flips the "immediate deletion" checkbox, unless it is
168	// locked or absent.
169	func (m *OptionConfirmModal) toggleCheckbox() {
170		if m.locked || m.hidden {
171			return
172		}
173		m.option = !m.option
174	}
175	
176	// handleConfirm handles confirmation based on the selected element
177	func (m *OptionConfirmModal) handleConfirm() (*OptionConfirmModal, tea.Cmd) {
178		switch m.focused {
179		case 0:
180			// Toggle checkbox
181			m.toggleCheckbox()
182			return m, nil
183		case 1:
184			// Yes
185			return m, func() tea.Msg {
186				return OptionConfirmModalYesMsg{Option: m.option}
187			}
188		case 2:
189			// No
190			return m, func() tea.Msg {
191				return OptionConfirmModalNoMsg{}
192			}
193		}
194		return m, nil
195	}
196	
197	// View renders the modal
198	func (m *OptionConfirmModal) View() string {
199		var b strings.Builder
200	
201		// Title
202		b.WriteString(theme.TitleStyle.Render(m.title))
203		b.WriteString("\n\n")
204	
205		// Message
206		b.WriteString(m.message)
207		b.WriteString("\n\n")
208	
209		// Checkbox for immediate deletion — absent when the option has no
210		// meaning on this backend (m.hidden), not merely greyed out.
211		if !m.hidden {

Done. Implementation summary:

**What was built** (branch `feat/setup-wizard`, committed as `bd6bdd4`):
- `internal/ui/setup/` — a standalone Bubble Tea wizard (`dk setup`): one form (Rule 112) covering context name, secret backend, container engine, theme, and forge (type/URL/namespace/visibility/clone method/optional token). Token entry validates live against the real API via `session.Auth.Authenticate` before being saved. Name collisions get a confirm-to-overwrite modal; a successful save offers to make the context active.
- `main.go` — reinstated exactly one CLI subcommand case (`setup`), with the removed-subcommand comment updated to explain the exception.
- Unit tests (`buildConfig`, cycle-field wrapping, the GitHub/`internal`-visibility coercion, overwrite/token-failure flows, and the real `config`/`credentials` I/O paths against a redirected `$HOME`).

**Verified:** `go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./...` (all packages), `golangci-lint run` (0 issues), `gofmt`. Binary runs and fails gracefully on this sandbox's missing `/dev/tty` — expected; a real interactive run needs to happen on your host terminal, since a real terminal is exactly what this sandbox can't offer (per this repo's own testing-split notes).

**Next steps are yours to run from the host** (this sandbox has no `entire://` auth, per this repo's host-relay workflow):
```bash
git push origin feat/setup-wizard
gh pr create -R anthnel/devdesk --base main --head feat/setup-wizard --fill
```
I'd also suggest actually walking through the wizard once in a real terminal (`go run . setup`) before merging, to confirm the on-screen layout and flow feel right — that's the one thing I couldn't check from here.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Most tasks are a single `go ...` invocation and run unchanged under both the
# POSIX shell and the "cmd /c" that mise defaults to on Windows. Tasks relying on
# POSIX syntax declare `shell = "bash -c"` explicitly — the global
# `windows_default_inline_shell_args` setting is refused from a project config.

[tools]
go = "1.25"
# Pinned so CI and every machine lint against the same rules. Without a pin, two
# golangci-lint versions disagree on what Rule 305 considers a clean run.
golangci-lint = "2.12.2"
# Pinned for the same reason, and it matters more here: goreleaser's own
# configuration schema changes between minor versions, so an unpinned tool
# would fail on `version: 2` syntax that was valid when it was written.
goreleaser = "2.18.0"
# Pinned for the same reason as the two above. Used by docs-serve/docs-build
# to run mkdocs-material without installing it as a mise tool: mkdocs-material
# is a theme/plugin package, not an app — it exposes no console-script entry
# point of its own (only its dependency `mkdocs` does), so `pipx:mkdocs-material`
# fails on every platform with "No executables are provided by package
# `mkdocs-material`". `uv tool run --with` sidesteps this by running `mkdocs`
# (which has an entry point) in an ephemeral environment with mkdocs-material
# injected alongside it.
uv = "0.12.10"

[tasks.build]
description = "Build the binary to bin/dk"
# `$(go env GOEXE)` for the same reason as [tasks.install]: `-o` takes the name
# literally, and PowerShell refuses to run an extension-less file even by
# explicit path — "Cannot run a document in the middle of a pipeline". Only
# `mise run run` uses this binary today, and it goes through bash, which is why
# nothing has complained. Empty on every other platform.
#
# Seule la version passe par -ldflags. Le commit et la date viennent des
# métadonnées que `-buildvcs=auto` embarque tout seul, et que
# `internal/version` lit en repli : les poser ici aussi serait une seconde
# source pour une réponse que le compilateur donne déjà. `git describe` sans
# `--always` échoue tant qu'aucun tag n'existe, et c'est voulu — un SHA promu
# au rang de numéro de version est pire que "dev".
shell = "bash -c"
run = '''
version=$(git describe --tags --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)
go build -ldflags "-X github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/version.version=$version" -o "bin/dk$(go env GOEXE)" .
'''

[tasks.run]
description = "Build and run the application"
depends = ["build"]
shell = "bash -c"
run = './bin/dk$(go env GOEXE)'

[tasks.dev]
description = "Run directly with go run (faster for development)"
run = "go run ."

[tasks.test]
description = "Run all tests"
run = "go test -v ./..."

[tasks.test-race]
description = "Run tests with race detector (requires a C toolchain: gcc/clang)"
env = { CGO_ENABLED = "1" }
run = "go test -race ./..."

[tasks.cover]
description = "Run tests and report coverage per package"
run = "go test -cover ./..."

[tasks.fmt]
description = "Format code"
run = "go fmt ./..."

[tasks.fmt-check]
description = "Fail when a file is not gofmt-clean (fmt rewrites, this one reports)"
shell = "bash -c"
run = """
unformatted=$(gofmt -l .)
if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then
  echo "not gofmt-clean:"
  echo "$unformatted"
  exit 1
fi
"""

[tasks.vet]
description = "Run go vet"
run = "go vet ./..."

[tasks.lint]
description = "Run golangci-lint"
run = "golangci-lint run"

[tasks.tidy]
description = "Tidy dependencies"
run = "go mod tidy"

[tasks.deps]
description = "Download dependencies"
run = "go mod download"

[tasks.clean]
description = "Clean build artifacts"
shell = "bash -c"
run = """
rm -rf bin
go clean
"""

[tasks.install]
description = "Install the dk binary to $GOPATH/bin"
# Two things a bare `go install` gets wrong here. It names the binary after the
# module (`devdesk`), while the command — and `mise run build` — is `dk`; and
# mise's go plugin exports GOBIN=<mise>/installs/go/<version>/bin, so the binary
# would land in a directory that disappears on the next toolchain bump.
#
# `go env GOEXE` is what `go install` would have appended, and dropping it is not
# cosmetic on Windows: `-o` takes the name literally, so the file lands as `dk`
# with no extension. It is a valid PE and runs by explicit path — which is why
# `mise run run` never noticed — but PowerShell and cmd resolve a bare command
# through PATHEXT, so `dk` is simply not found. GOEXE is empty everywhere else.
#
# The destination is printed rather than tested. Whether `dk` will resolve is a
# question about the *calling* shell's PATH, and this task runs under bash: a
# check here would answer for the wrong shell and be believed. Saying where the
# binary went lets the reader answer it themselves, which is the one thing a
# "command not found" a second later does not tell them.
shell = "bash -c"
run = """
target="$(go env GOPATH)/bin/dk$(go env GOEXE)"
version=$(git describe --tags --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)
go build -ldflags "-X github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/version.version=$version" -o "$target" .
echo "installed $target"
echo "run it as 'dk' once $(dirname "$target") is on PATH"
"""

[tasks.release-check]
description = "Validate .goreleaser.yaml without building anything"
run = "goreleaser check"

[tasks.release]
description = "Build the release artifacts and attach them to the GitHub Release (CI only)"
# Needs GITHUB_TOKEN and a tag; it is the release workflow's build step, and
# running it by hand would publish. `release-snapshot` is the local equivalent.
run = "goreleaser release --clean"

[tasks.release-snapshot]
description = "Build the release artifacts locally, publishing nothing"
# `--snapshot` is what makes this runnable without a tag: goreleaser invents a
# version rather than refusing. It is the only way to find out that a build
# target is broken before a tag has been pushed, which is the point at which
# the mistake is expensive.
run = "goreleaser release --snapshot --clean"

[tasks.check]
description = "Run fmt, vet, lint and tests (pre-commit checklist)"
depends = ["fmt", "vet", "lint", "test"]

[tasks.docs-serve]
description = "Preview the documentation site locally"
shell = "bash -c"
# Same changelog staging step as docs-build — without it, mkdocs.yml's nav
# points at a changelog.md that doesn't exist yet on a fresh checkout.
run = """
cp CHANGELOG.md docs-site/docs/changelog.md
uv tool run --with mkdocs-material==9.6.14 mkdocs serve -f docs-site/mkdocs.yml
"""

[tasks.docs-build]
description = "Build the static documentation site into docs-site/site"
shell = "bash -c"
# CHANGELOG.md is copied in rather than symlinked so the build works the same
# way locally and in CI, on every OS mise supports.
# --site-dir is resolved relative to the config file (-f), not the cwd: passing
# "docs-site/site" here built into docs-site/docs-site/site instead, so
# actions/upload-pages-artifact found nothing at docs-site/site in CI.
run = """
cp CHANGELOG.md docs-site/docs/changelog.md
uv tool run --with mkdocs-material==9.6.14 mkdocs build -f docs-site/mkdocs.yml --site-dir site
"""

package theme

import (
	"strings"

	"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/table"
	"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
	"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
)

// Layout styles
var (
	HeaderStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
			Background(ColorBackground).
			Bold(false)

	HeaderKeyStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
			Background(ColorBackground).
			Foreground(ColorHeaderKey).
			Bold(true)

	HeaderValueStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
				Background(ColorBackground).
				Foreground(ColorPrimary).
				Bold(true)

	CommandLineStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
				Background(ColorCmdLineBg).
				Foreground(ColorCmdLineFg).
				Padding(0, 1, 0, 1)

	CommandLineInactiveStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
					Background(ColorBackground).
					Foreground(ColorCmdLineInactiveFg).
					Padding(0, 1, 0, 1)

	ShortcutKeyStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
				Background(ColorBackground).
				Foreground(ColorSecondary).
				Bold(true)

	// ShortcutKeyDisabledStyle: the key of a shortcut that is shown but has
	// no purpose here (Rule 130). It loses the color *and* the boldness —
	// either alone would leave a bold gray, which reads as emphasis.
	ShortcutKeyDisabledStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
					Background(ColorBackground).
					Foreground(ColorShortcutDisabled).
					Bold(false)

	ShortcutDescriptionStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
					Background(ColorBackground).
					Foreground(ColorDim).
					Bold(false)

	TitleStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
			Background(ColorBackground).
			Foreground(ColorTitleFg).
			Bold(true)

	// View subtitle style
	SubTitleStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
			Background(ColorBackground).
			Foreground(ColorSubTitleFg).
			Bold(true)
)

// Status styles
var (
	StatusOKStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
			Background(ColorBackground).
			Foreground(ColorOK).
			Bold(true)

	StatusDownStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
			Background(ColorBackground).
			Foreground(ColorError).
			Bold(true)

	StatusErrorStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
				Background(ColorBackground).
				Foreground(ColorError).
				Bold(true)

	StatusWarningStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
				Background(ColorBackground).
				Foreground(ColorWarn).
				Bold(true)
)

// Footer message styles, one per level (Rule 128).
//
// Info is not bold, the other two are: the hierarchy runs through weight as
// well as hue, and a neutral notice rendered bold would read as an alert again
// — which is what the yellow ColorHighlight line did before.
//
// Nothing outside components.FooterMessage should use these. They exist as
// exported styles so a theme change refreshes them like every other style, not
// so a view can render its own footer line.
var (
	FooterInfoStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
			Background(ColorBackground).
			Foreground(ColorFooterInfo).
			Bold(false)

	FooterWarnStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
			Background(ColorBackground).
			Foreground(ColorFooterWarn).
			Bold(true)

	FooterErrorStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
				Background(ColorBackground).
				Foreground(ColorFooterError).
				Bold(true)
)

// Component styles
var (
	KeyStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
			Background(ColorBackground).
			Foreground(ColorHighlight).
			Bold(true)

	PausedStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
			Background(ColorBackground).
			Foreground(ColorError).
			Bold(true)

	DimStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
			Background(ColorBackground).
			Foreground(ColorDim).
			Bold(false)

	HelpStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
			Background(ColorBackground).
			Foreground(ColorDim).
			Italic(true)
)

var (
	PrimaryColorStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().
				Background(ColorBackground).

14	// View renders the wizard: the form, or whichever overlay is active on top
15	// of it (Rule 112 — a confirmation is a centered modal, never the viewport).
16	func (m Model) View() string {
17		switch m.stage {
18		case stageConfirmOverwrite, stageConfirmSetCurrent:
19			return lipgloss.Place(m.width, m.height, lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center,
20				m.confirmModal.View(),
21				lipgloss.WithWhitespaceBackground(theme.ColorBackground))
22		case stageDone:
23			return m.renderDone()
24		default:
25			return m.renderForm()
26		}
27	}
28	
29	func (m Model) renderForm() string {
30		var b strings.Builder
31	
32		b.WriteString(theme.TitleStyle.Render("DevDesk setup — new context"))
33		b.WriteString("\n")
34		b.WriteString(theme.EmptyLineBg(m.width) + "\n")
35	
36		v := forge.VocabularyFor(config.ForgeTypes()[m.forgeTypeIdx])
37	
38		fields := []string{
39			renderTextField("Context name", m.contextNameInput.View(), m.focusedField == fieldContextName),
40			renderCycleField("Secret backend", secretBackendOptions[m.secretBackendIdx], m.focusedField == fieldSecretBackend),
41			renderCycleField("Container engine", config.ContainerEngines()[m.containerEngineIdx], m.focusedField == fieldContainerEngine),
42			renderCycleField("Theme", m.themeOptions[m.themeIdx], m.focusedField == fieldTheme),
43			renderCycleField("Forge", v.Name, m.focusedField == fieldForgeType),
44			renderTextField(v.Name+" URL", m.forgeURLInput.View(), m.focusedField == fieldForgeURL),
45			renderTextField("Default "+v.Namespace, m.forgeNamespaceInput.View(), m.focusedField == fieldForgeNamespace),
46			renderCycleField("Visibility", m.visibilityValue, m.focusedField == fieldForgeVisibility),
47			renderCycleField("Clone method", cloneMethodOptions[m.cloneMethodIdx], m.focusedField == fieldForgeCloneMethod),
48			renderTextField(v.TokenLabel, m.forgeTokenInput.View(), m.focusedField == fieldForgeToken),
49		}
50		for _, f := range fields {
51			b.WriteString(f)
52			b.WriteString("\n\n")
53		}
54	
55		b.WriteString("  " + theme.RenderButton("Create context", m.focusedField == fieldSubmit, "primary"))
56		b.WriteString("\n\n")
57	
58		b.WriteString(m.footer.View(m.width, m.status()))
59		b.WriteString("\n")
60		b.WriteString(theme.HelpStyle.Render("  [↑↓] navigate  [←→] change  [enter] confirm  [esc] quit"))
61	
62		return b.String()
63	}
64	
65	func (m Model) renderDone() string {
66		var b strings.Builder
67	
68		b.WriteString(theme.TitleStyle.Render("Context ready"))
69		b.WriteString("\n\n")
70		b.WriteString(theme.Bg("Wrote " + m.savedPath))
71		b.WriteString("\n")
72		if m.currentContextWarning != "" {
73			b.WriteString(lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorError).
74				Render(m.currentContextWarning))
75			b.WriteString("\n")
76		}
77		b.WriteString("\n")
78		b.WriteString(theme.Bg(`Run "dk" to start.`))
79		b.WriteString("\n\n")
80		b.WriteString(theme.HelpStyle.Render("  [enter] exit"))
81	
82		return b.String()
83	}

85	func (m Model) status() components.Status {
86		if m.pending != "" {
87			return components.Status{Text: m.pending, Spinner: true}
88		}
89		return components.Status{}
90	}

92	// renderTextField renders a single-line label over a textinput's view,
93	// following Rule 120: the focus indicator and chevron separator, no ":".
94	func renderTextField(label, valueView string, focused bool) string {
95		var labelStr string
96		if focused {
97			labelStr = theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " " + label + " " + theme.IconChevronRight)
98		} else {
99			labelStr = theme.Bg("  " + label + " " + theme.IconChevronRight)
100		}
101		return labelStr + "\n" + theme.Bg("  ") + valueView
102	}
103	
104	// renderCycleField renders a closed-set field with the ←→ cycle pattern
105	// (Rule 132), the same layout CreationForm's resource-type field uses.
106	func renderCycleField(label, value string, focused bool) string {
107		selectLabel := label + " " + theme.IconSelect + " "
108		valueView := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).Render(value)
109		if focused {
110			return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + valueView
111		}
112		return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + valueView
113	}

2	// that walks a user through creating (or overwriting) a DevDesk context. It
3	// is not part of the app router — it runs before any context is loaded, so
4	// it builds a *config.Config from scratch and writes it with
5	// config.SaveContext, the same call the configuration view uses.
6	package setup
7	
8	import (

10		"strings"
11	
12		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
13		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
14		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
15	
16		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
17		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge"
18		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
19		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
20	)
21	
22	// Field indices, top to bottom, matching the order rendered in View.
23	const (
24		fieldContextName = iota
25		fieldSecretBackend
26		fieldContainerEngine
27		fieldTheme
28		fieldForgeType
29		fieldForgeURL
30		fieldForgeNamespace
31		fieldForgeVisibility
32		fieldForgeCloneMethod
33		fieldForgeToken
34		fieldSubmit
35	)
36	
37	// secretBackendOptions mirrors config.AppConfig.SecretBackend's closed set.
38	var secretBackendOptions = []string{"auto", "keyring", "git-credential"}
39	
40	// cloneMethodOptions mirrors config.ForgeConfig.CloneMethod's closed set.
41	var cloneMethodOptions = []string{"https", "ssh"}
42	
43	// stage tracks what the wizard is doing once every field has a value.
44	type stage int
45	
46	const (
47		stageForm stage = iota
48		stageConfirmOverwrite
49		stageConfirmSetCurrent
50		stageDone
51	)
52	
53	// modalPurpose says what a Yes/No answer on the active confirm modal means —
54	// the wizard reuses one ConfirmModal for both of its confirmations rather
55	// than declaring two near-identical fields.
56	type modalPurpose int
57	
58	const (
59		modalNone modalPurpose = iota
60		modalOverwrite
61		modalSetCurrent
62	)
63	
64	// Model is the wizard: one form, top to bottom (Rule 112), that ends by
65	// writing a context via config.SaveContext.
66	type Model struct {
67		width, height int
68	
69		focusedField int
70		stage        stage
71		modalPurpose modalPurpose
72		confirmModal *components.ConfirmModal
73	
74		contextNameInput textinput.Model
75	
76		secretBackendIdx   int
77		containerEngineIdx int
78	
79		themeOptions []string
80		themeIdx     int
81	
82		forgeTypeIdx int
83		// forgeURLTouched stops the URL field from being overwritten once the user
84		// has typed into it, so switching Forge back and forth does not clobber a
85		// self-hosted URL they already entered.
86		forgeURLTouched     bool
87		forgeURLInput       textinput.Model
88		forgeNamespaceInput textinput.Model
89		visibilityValue     string
90		cloneMethodIdx      int
91		forgeTokenInput     textinput.Model
92	
93		// pending names the async step in flight, shown in the footer with a
94		// spinner (Rule 128); empty when nothing is running.
95		pending string
96		footer  components.FooterMessage
97		spinner spinner.Model
98	
99		savedPath             string
100		currentContextWarning string
101	}
102	
103	// New builds the wizard with every field at its default value.
104	func New() Model {
105		nameInput := textinput.New()
106		nameInput.Placeholder = "e.g. work, staging"
107		nameInput.CharLimit = 64
108		nameInput.Width = 40
109		styleTextInput(&nameInput)
110		nameInput.Focus()
111	
112		urlInput := textinput.New()
113		urlInput.CharLimit = 200
114		urlInput.Width = 50
115		styleTextInput(&urlInput)
116	
117		nsInput := textinput.New()
118		nsInput.Placeholder = "optional"
119		nsInput.CharLimit = 100
120		nsInput.Width = 40
121		styleTextInput(&nsInput)
122	
123		tokenInput := textinput.New()
124		tokenInput.Placeholder = "optional — can be set later via the auth view"
125		tokenInput.CharLimit = 200
126		tokenInput.Width = 50
127		tokenInput.EchoMode = textinput.EchoPassword
128		styleTextInput(&tokenInput)
129	
130		themes, err := theme.ListThemes()
131		if err != nil || len(themes) == 0 {
132			themes = []string{"default"}
133		}
134	
135		s := spinner.New()
136		s.Spinner = spinner.Dot
137		s.Style = spinnerStyle
138	
139		m := Model{
140			focusedField:        fieldContextName,
141			contextNameInput:    nameInput,
142			themeOptions:        themes,
143			forgeURLInput:       urlInput,
144			forgeNamespaceInput: nsInput,
145			visibilityValue:     "private",
146			forgeTokenInput:     tokenInput,
147			spinner:             s,
148		}
149		m.forgeURLInput.SetValue(forge.VocabularyFor(config.ForgeTypes()[m.forgeTypeIdx]).ExampleURL)
150		return m
151	}
152	
153	// Init starts the cursor blink, the only thing the wizard needs on launch.
154	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
155		return textinput.Blink
156	}
157	
158	// Update is the single Elm-architecture entry point (Rule 110): every field
159	// mutation happens here, never inside a Cmd.
160	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
161		switch msg := msg.(type) {
162		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
163			m.width = msg.Width
164			m.height = msg.Height
165			return m, nil
166	
167		case tea.KeyMsg:
168			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
169	
170		case spinner.TickMsg:
171			var cmd tea.Cmd
172			m.spinner, cmd = m.spinner.Update(msg)
173			m.footer.SetSpinnerFrame(m.spinner.View())
174			return m, cmd
175	
176		case components.ConfirmModalYesMsg:
177			return m.handleConfirmYes()
178	
179		case components.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
180			return m.handleConfirmNo()
181	
182		case ContextExistsMsg:
183			return m.handleContextExists(msg)
184	
185		case TokenValidatedMsg:

187	
188		case ContextSavedMsg:
189			return m.handleContextSaved(msg)
190	
191		case CurrentContextSetMsg:
192			return m.handleCurrentContextSet(msg)
193		}
194	
195		if m.footer.Handle(msg) {
196			return m, nil
197		}
198		return m, nil
199	}
200	
201	func (m Model) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
202		if m.stage == stageConfirmOverwrite || m.stage == stageConfirmSetCurrent {
203			var cmd tea.Cmd

## Summary

**No remote/network theme-import mechanism exists anywhere in this codebase — it is not implemented, and there is no documentation, backlog entry, or planned feature for it.** Themes are purely local, static JSON files.

### 1. `internal/ui/theme/manager.go` — full read

- `ThemeDir()` (`internal/ui/theme/manager.go:159-165`): returns `~/.devdesk/themes/`. No URL, no config for a remote source.
- `LoadTheme(name)` (`:168-190`): reads `ThemeDir()/<name>.json` via `os.ReadFile` and `json.Unmarshal`. Purely local filesystem. `""`, `"dark"`, `"default"` map to the built-in `DefaultTheme()`.
- `ListThemes()` (`:193-215`): starts with `[]string{"default"}`, then lists `*.json` files in `ThemeDir()` via `os.ReadDir`. No network call, no caching, no "registry index" concept.
- There is **no** function anywhere in this file (or package) for downloading, fetching, importing from a URL, or pushing/sharing a theme. The only I/O primitives used are `os.ReadFile` / `os.ReadDir` / `os.UserHomeDir`.

### 2. Repo-wide keyword search

`grep -rniE "import theme|theme gallery|theme repositor|share theme|download theme|remote theme|theme registry|online theme|fetch theme|theme url"` across `*.go` and `*.md` returned **zero hits**. Nothing in `docs/`, `README.md`, `.claude/`, or `internal/ui/theme/` mentions any network-based theme distribution concept.

### 3. `docs/architecture/*.md`

No architecture doc is dedicated to the theme system. `docs/architecture/configuration.md:9` and `:134,178` only mention theme as one of the cycle-fields in the settings view (App-level setting, applies live on cycle rather than on blur). `docs/backlog.md` has extensive theme history (search results at lines ~1865-1911), most notably:
- A `:theme` command/picker used to exist (`internal/app/theme.go`, `CommandTheme`, `ThemeListMsg`/`ThemeAppliedMsg`/`ThemeErrorMsg`) but was **deliberately removed** (§3.9 in backlog) because it was a second, disk-writing path that duplicated the configuration view's own field — nothing to do with network import, purely a local-picker consolidation.
- `docs/backlog.md:13018-13021`: confirms the 12 bundled themes in `themes/` are files "copiés par l'utilisateur dans `~/.devdesk/themes/`" (copied by the user) — reinforcing the manual-copy-only model.

### 4. `internal/ui/configuration` (settings view)

`internal/ui/configuration/fields.go:227` defines the Theme field as a `cycle(...)` field bound directly to `c.App.Theme`, populated from `theme.ListThemes()` (called in `model.go:113`). It is a left/right cycle through whatever `.json` files already sit in `~/.devdesk/themes/` — no "browse online themes," no fetch/import action, no HTTP client wired in. `update.go:255-259` shows the theme's only special behavior is applying live instead of on blur; still no network involvement.

### 5. `go.mod`

1	// Package setup implements `dk setup`: a small standalone Bubble Tea program
2	// that walks a user through creating (or overwriting) a DevDesk context. It
3	// is not part of the app router — it runs before any context is loaded, so
4	// it builds a *config.Config from scratch and writes it with
5	// config.SaveContext, the same call the configuration view uses.
6	package setup
7	
8	import (
9		"log"
10		"strings"
11	
12		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
13		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
14		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
15	
16		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
17		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge"
18		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
19		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
20	)
21	
22	// Field indices, top to bottom, matching the order rendered in View.
23	const (
24		fieldContextName = iota
25		fieldSecretBackend
26		fieldContainerEngine
27		fieldTheme
28		fieldForgeType
29		fieldForgeURL
30		fieldForgeNamespace
31		fieldForgeVisibility
32		fieldForgeCloneMethod
33		fieldForgeToken
34		fieldSubmit
35	)
36	
37	// secretBackendOptions mirrors config.AppConfig.SecretBackend's closed set.
38	var secretBackendOptions = []string{"auto", "keyring", "git-credential"}
39	
40	// cloneMethodOptions mirrors config.ForgeConfig.CloneMethod's closed set.
41	var cloneMethodOptions = []string{"https", "ssh"}
42	
43	// stage tracks what the wizard is doing once every field has a value.
44	type stage int
45	
46	const (
47		stageForm stage = iota
48		stageConfirmOverwrite
49		stageConfirmSetCurrent
50		stageDone
51	)
52	
53	// modalPurpose says what a Yes/No answer on the active confirm modal means —
54	// the wizard reuses one ConfirmModal for both of its confirmations rather
55	// than declaring two near-identical fields.
56	type modalPurpose int
57	
58	const (
59		modalNone modalPurpose = iota
60		modalOverwrite
61		modalSetCurrent
62	)
63	
64	// Model is the wizard: one form, top to bottom (Rule 112), that ends by
65	// writing a context via config.SaveContext.
66	type Model struct {
67		width, height int
68	
69		focusedField int
70		stage        stage
71		modalPurpose modalPurpose
72		confirmModal *components.ConfirmModal
73	
74		contextNameInput textinput.Model
75	
76		secretBackendIdx   int
77		containerEngineIdx int
78	
79		themeOptions []string
80		themeIdx     int
81	
82		forgeTypeIdx int
83		// forgeURLTouched stops the URL field from being overwritten once the user
84		// has typed into it, so switching Forge back and forth does not clobber a
85		// self-hosted URL they already entered.
86		forgeURLTouched     bool
87		forgeURLInput       textinput.Model
88		forgeNamespaceInput textinput.Model
89		visibilityValue     string
90		cloneMethodIdx      int
91		forgeTokenInput     textinput.Model
92	
93		// pending names the async step in flight, shown in the footer with a
94		// spinner (Rule 128); empty when nothing is running.
95		pending string
96		footer  components.FooterMessage
97		spinner spinner.Model
98	
99		savedPath             string
100		currentContextWarning string
101	}

103	// New builds the wizard with every field at its default value.
104	func New() Model {
105		nameInput := textinput.New()
106		nameInput.Placeholder = "e.g. work, staging"
107		nameInput.CharLimit = 64
108		nameInput.Width = 40
109		styleTextInput(&nameInput)
110		nameInput.Focus()
111	
112		urlInput := textinput.New()
113		urlInput.CharLimit = 200
114		urlInput.Width = 50
115		styleTextInput(&urlInput)
116	
117		nsInput := textinput.New()
118		nsInput.Placeholder = "optional"
119		nsInput.CharLimit = 100
120		nsInput.Width = 40
121		styleTextInput(&nsInput)
122	
123		tokenInput := textinput.New()
124		tokenInput.Placeholder = "optional — can be set later via the auth view"
125		tokenInput.CharLimit = 200
126		tokenInput.Width = 50
127		tokenInput.EchoMode = textinput.EchoPassword
128		styleTextInput(&tokenInput)
129	
130		themes, err := theme.ListThemes()
131		if err != nil || len(themes) == 0 {
132			themes = []string{"default"}
133		}
134	
135		s := spinner.New()
136		s.Spinner = spinner.Dot
137		s.Style = spinnerStyle
138	
139		m := Model{
140			focusedField:        fieldContextName,
141			contextNameInput:    nameInput,
142			themeOptions:        themes,
143			forgeURLInput:       urlInput,
144			forgeNamespaceInput: nsInput,
145			visibilityValue:     "private",
146			forgeTokenInput:     tokenInput,

150		return m
151	}

153	// Init starts the cursor blink, the only thing the wizard needs on launch.
154	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
155		return textinput.Blink
156	}
157	
158	// Update is the single Elm-architecture entry point (Rule 110): every field
159	// mutation happens here, never inside a Cmd.
160	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
161		switch msg := msg.(type) {
162		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
163			m.width = msg.Width
164			m.height = msg.Height
165			return m, nil
166	
167		case tea.KeyMsg:
168			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
169	
170		case spinner.TickMsg:
171			var cmd tea.Cmd
172			m.spinner, cmd = m.spinner.Update(msg)
173			return m, cmd
174	
175		case components.ConfirmModalYesMsg:
176			return m.handleConfirmYes()
177	
178		case components.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
179			return m.handleConfirmNo()
180	
181		case ContextExistsMsg:
182			return m.handleContextExists(msg)
183	
184		case TokenValidatedMsg:
185			return m.handleTokenValidated(msg)
186	
187		case ContextSavedMsg:
188			return m.handleContextSaved(msg)
189	
190		case CurrentContextSetMsg:
191			return m.handleCurrentContextSet(msg)
192		}
193	
194		if m.footer.Handle(msg) {
195			return m, nil
196		}
197		return m, nil
198	}
199	
200	func (m Model) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
201		if m.stage == stageConfirmOverwrite || m.stage == stageConfirmSetCurrent {
202			var cmd tea.Cmd
203			m.confirmModal, cmd = m.confirmModal.Update(msg)
204			return m, cmd
205		}
206		if m.stage == stageDone {
207			if msg.String() == "enter" || msg.String() == "esc" || msg.String() == "q" {
208				return m, tea.Quit
209			}
210			return m, nil
211		}
212	
213		switch msg.String() {
214		case "ctrl+c":
215			return m, tea.Quit
216		case "esc":
217			return m, tea.Quit
218		case "up":
219			m.moveFocus(-1)
220			return m, nil
221		case "down":
222			m.moveFocus(1)
223			return m, nil
224		case "left":
225			m.cycle(-1)
226			return m, nil
227		case "right":
228			m.cycle(1)
229			return m, nil
230		case "enter":
231			if m.focusedField == fieldSubmit {
232				return m.submit()
233			}
234			m.moveFocus(1)
235			return m, nil
236		}
237	
238		return m.updateFocusedInput(msg)
239	}
240	
241	// moveFocus walks the field list, wrapping at both ends — the same shape
242	// CreationForm uses, and consistent with Rule 111 having no "past the edge"
243	// state to fall into.
244	func (m *Model) moveFocus(delta int) {
245		m.focusedField = wrap(m.focusedField+delta, fieldSubmit+1)
246		m.updateFocus()
247	}
248	
249	func (m *Model) updateFocus() {
250		m.contextNameInput.Blur()
251		m.forgeURLInput.Blur()
252		m.forgeNamespaceInput.Blur()
253		m.forgeTokenInput.Blur()
254	
255		switch m.focusedField {
256		case fieldContextName:
257			m.contextNameInput.Focus()
258		case fieldForgeURL:
259			m.forgeURLInput.Focus()
260		case fieldForgeNamespace:
261			m.forgeNamespaceInput.Focus()
262		case fieldForgeToken:
263			m.forgeTokenInput.Focus()
264		}
265	}
266	
267	// cycle changes a closed-set field's value (Rule 132). On any other field —
268	// including a text field, where left/right have no role here (matching
269	// CreationForm's name/description fields) — it does nothing.
270	func (m *Model) cycle(delta int) {
271		switch m.focusedField {
272		case fieldSecretBackend:
273			m.secretBackendIdx = wrap(m.secretBackendIdx+delta, len(secretBackendOptions))
274		case fieldContainerEngine:
275			m.containerEngineIdx = wrap(m.containerEngineIdx+delta, len(config.ContainerEngines()))
276		case fieldTheme:
277			m.themeIdx = wrap(m.themeIdx+delta, len(m.themeOptions))
278		case fieldForgeType:
279			m.forgeTypeIdx = wrap(m.forgeTypeIdx+delta, len(config.ForgeTypes()))
280			m.onForgeTypeChanged()
281		case fieldForgeVisibility:
282			opts := m.visibilityOptions()
283			idx := indexOf(opts, m.visibilityValue)
284			if idx < 0 {
285				idx = 0
286			}
287			m.visibilityValue = opts[wrap(idx+delta, len(opts))]
288		case fieldForgeCloneMethod:
289			m.cloneMethodIdx = wrap(m.cloneMethodIdx+delta, len(cloneMethodOptions))
290		}
291	}
292	
293	// onForgeTypeChanged keeps the URL placeholder and the visibility value
294	// consistent with the newly selected forge.
295	func (m *Model) onForgeTypeChanged() {
296		forgeType := config.ForgeTypes()[m.forgeTypeIdx]
297		if !m.forgeURLTouched {
298			m.forgeURLInput.SetValue(forge.VocabularyFor(forgeType).ExampleURL)
299		}
300		// GitHub has no "internal" visibility. Coerced to the most private option
301		// rather than clamped by position — clamping "internal" (index 1 of 3)
302		// into a 2-option list would land on "public", the opposite of safe.
303		if indexOf(m.visibilityOptions(), m.visibilityValue) < 0 {
304			m.visibilityValue = "private"
305		}
306	}

308	// visibilityOptions is the closed set config.ForgeConfig.DefaultVisibility
309	// accepts for the currently selected forge type.
310	func (m Model) visibilityOptions() []string {
311		if config.ForgeTypes()[m.forgeTypeIdx] == config.ForgeGitHub {
312			return []string{"private", "public"}
313		}
314		return []string{"private", "internal", "public"}
315	}

317	func (m Model) updateFocusedInput(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
318		var cmd tea.Cmd
319		switch m.focusedField {
320		case fieldContextName:
321			m.contextNameInput, cmd = m.contextNameInput.Update(msg)
322		case fieldForgeURL:
323			m.forgeURLTouched = true
324			m.forgeURLInput, cmd = m.forgeURLInput.Update(msg)
325		case fieldForgeNamespace:
326			m.forgeNamespaceInput, cmd = m.forgeNamespaceInput.Update(msg)
327		case fieldForgeToken:
328			m.forgeTokenInput, cmd = m.forgeTokenInput.Update(msg)
329		}
330		return m, cmd
331	}

333	func wrap(i, n int) int {
334		if n <= 0 {
335			return 0
336		}
337		return ((i % n) + n) % n
338	}
339	
340	func indexOf(opts []string, v string) int {
341		for i, o := range opts {
342			if o == v {
343				return i
344			}
345		}
346		return -1
347	}

349	// submit validates the context name and starts the async chain: existence
350	// check, then (if a token was entered) validation, then the write itself.
351	func (m Model) submit() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
352		name := strings.TrimSpace(m.contextNameInput.Value())
353		if err := config.ValidateContextName(name); err != nil {
354			return m, m.footer.Error(err.Error())
355		}
356		m.contextNameInput.SetValue(name)
357		m.pending = "Checking context name..."
358		return m, checkContextExistsCmd(name)
359	}

361	func (m Model) handleContextExists(msg ContextExistsMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
362		m.pending = ""
363		if msg.Err != nil {
364			log.Printf("ERROR [setup] check context exists: %v", msg.Err)
365			return m, m.footer.Error("Failed to check context: " + msg.Err.Error())
366		}
367		if msg.Exists {
368			name := strings.TrimSpace(m.contextNameInput.Value())
369			m.confirmModal = components.NewConfirmModal("Context exists",
370				"Context '"+name+"' already exists and will be overwritten. Continue?")
371			m.stage = stageConfirmOverwrite
372			m.modalPurpose = modalOverwrite
373			return m, nil
374		}
375		return m.proceedAfterNameConfirmed()
376	}

378	func (m Model) handleConfirmYes() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
379		purpose := m.modalPurpose
380		m.confirmModal = nil
381		m.stage = stageForm
382		m.modalPurpose = modalNone
383	
384		switch purpose {
385		case modalOverwrite:
386			return m.proceedAfterNameConfirmed()
387		case modalSetCurrent:
388			m.pending = "Setting current context..."
389			return m, setCurrentContextCmd(strings.TrimSpace(m.contextNameInput.Value()))
390		}

392	}

396		m.confirmModal = nil
397		m.stage = stageForm
398		m.modalPurpose = modalNone

402			// Back to the name field to pick a different one, rather than
403			// aborting the whole wizard over one collision.
404			m.focusedField = fieldContextName
405			m.updateFocus()
406			return m, nil
407		case modalSetCurrent:

412	}

## Summary

**No remote/network theme-import mechanism exists anywhere in this codebase — it is not implemented, and there is no documentation, backlog entry, or planned feature for it.** Themes are purely local, static JSON files.

### 1. `internal/ui/theme/manager.go` — full read

- `ThemeDir()` (`internal/ui/theme/manager.go:159-165`): returns `~/.devdesk/themes/`. No URL, no config for a remote source.
- `LoadTheme(name)` (`:168-190`): reads `ThemeDir()/<name>.json` via `os.ReadFile` and `json.Unmarshal`. Purely local filesystem. `""`, `"dark"`, `"default"` map to the built-in `DefaultTheme()`.
- `ListThemes()` (`:193-215`): starts with `[]string{"default"}`, then lists `*.json` files in `ThemeDir()` via `os.ReadDir`. No network call, no caching, no "registry index" concept.
- There is **no** function anywhere in this file (or package) for downloading, fetching, importing from a URL, or pushing/sharing a theme. The only I/O primitives used are `os.ReadFile` / `os.ReadDir` / `os.UserHomeDir`.

### 2. Repo-wide keyword search

`grep -rniE "import theme|theme gallery|theme repositor|share theme|download theme|remote theme|theme registry|online theme|fetch theme|theme url"` across `*.go` and `*.md` returned **zero hits**. Nothing in `docs/`, `README.md`, `.claude/`, or `internal/ui/theme/` mentions any network-based theme distribution concept.

### 3. `docs/architecture/*.md`

No architecture doc is dedicated to the theme system. `docs/architecture/configuration.md:9` and `:134,178` only mention theme as one of the cycle-fields in the settings view (App-level setting, applies live on cycle rather than on blur). `docs/backlog.md` has extensive theme history (search results at lines ~1865-1911), most notably:
- A `:theme` command/picker used to exist (`internal/app/theme.go`, `CommandTheme`, `ThemeListMsg`/`ThemeAppliedMsg`/`ThemeErrorMsg`) but was **deliberately removed** (§3.9 in backlog) because it was a second, disk-writing path that duplicated the configuration view's own field — nothing to do with network import, purely a local-picker consolidation.
- `docs/backlog.md:13018-13021`: confirms the 12 bundled themes in `themes/` are files "copiés par l'utilisateur dans `~/.devdesk/themes/`" (copied by the user) — reinforcing the manual-copy-only model.

### 4. `internal/ui/configuration` (settings view)

`internal/ui/configuration/fields.go:227` defines the Theme field as a `cycle(...)` field bound directly to `c.App.Theme`, populated from `theme.ListThemes()` (called in `model.go:113`). It is a left/right cycle through whatever `.json` files already sit in `~/.devdesk/themes/` — no "browse online themes," no fetch/import action, no HTTP client wired in. `update.go:255-259` shows the theme's only special behavior is applying live instead of on blur; still no network involvement.

### 5. `go.mod`

No dependency suggests a planned theme registry/gallery. HTTP-capable deps present (`golang.org/x/net`, `golang.org/x/oauth2`, `github.com/google/go-github/v68`, `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go`) are all for forge integration (GitHub/GitLab APIs), not theming. `internal/oci/oci.go` (mentioned in `docs/architecture/network.md`) is an OCI-registry HTTP client for container images — unrelated to themes, and nothing wires it (or anything else) to theme fetching. There's also `internal/netcheck` (`internal/netcheck/*.go`), a full diagnostics pipeline (resolve/route/reach/connect/TLS/HTTP checks) used by the Network Diagnostics view — this is the closest thing to a "check if a connection is available" primitive in the repo, but it targets a specific host:port for diagnostics, is not wired into `internal/ui/setup`, and has nothing to do with theme sources.

### 6. Exact Theme JSON schema

Struct: `internal/ui/theme/manager.go:14-83` (`type Theme struct`). Fields (JSON tags), required (no `omitempty`) first:
```
name, color_ok, color_error, color_warn, color_primary, color_secondary,
color_border, color_text, color_dim, color_highlight, color_white,
color_black, color_background
```
Then optional (`omitempty`): `title_fg, app_title_fg, subtitle_fg, button_fg, button_bg, button_inactive_fg, button_inactive_bg, tab_active_fg, tab_active_bg, tab_inactive_fg, tab_inactive_bg, table_header_fg, table_selected_fg, table_selected_bg, table_line_selected, cmd_line_fg, cmd_line_bg, cmd_line_inactive_fg, viewport_border, severity_critical(+_fg), severity_high(+_fg), severity_medium(+_fg), severity_low(+_fg), severity_info(+_fg), icon_namespace, icon_repository, icon_vis_public, icon_vis_internal, icon_vis_private, icon_directory, icon_file, icon_image`.

Example file: `themes/catppuccin-macchiato.json` (also `themes/{catppuccin-mocha,catppuccin-latte,catppuccin-frappe,tokyo-night,one-dark,dark-plus,nord,solarized-dark,solarized-light,github-dark,github-light}.json` — 12 total, all in repo root `themes/`, not shipped to `~/.devdesk/themes/` automatically).

### Current exact mechanism for a user to add a custom theme
Purely manual, local-file based (documented in `README.md:148-164`):
1. Author or copy a theme JSON matching the `Theme` struct schema above.
2. Place it at `~/.devdesk/themes/<name>.json` (`ThemeDir()`, `internal/ui/theme/manager.go:159`).
3. It then appears automatically in `ListThemes()`'s output and thus in the `:config` view's Theme cycle field, or can be set directly via `app.theme: <name>` in the config file (no `.json` suffix).

There is no download, no in-app fetch, no gallery browser, and no existing partial/experimental scaffolding for one — so designing the "theme" wizard question to offer network import vs. pointing to docs for manual import would be a wholly new feature, not something plugging into an existing (even if unfinished) mechanism.</result>
