git add internal/ui/setup/ internal/ui/vocabtest/ && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat: turn the setup wizard into one question at a time

Replace the single all-fields-at-once form with a step-by-step flow:
each question gets its own screen with an explanation of what the
choice means and its trade-offs, instead of a bare cycle field or text
box. Enter answers the current question and moves to the next; Esc
goes back one question (or quits from the first one).

Two new things came out of that redesign:

- A terminal font check is now the very first screen: it renders a
  sample of the Nerd Font glyphs used throughout the app and asks
  whether they look right. It is purely informational — nothing it
  answers is persisted or blocks continuing — so a broken font is
  caught before the rest of the wizard (and the app) becomes hard to
  read, not discovered by accident.

- The theme question now makes a single best-effort attempt to fetch
  the themes bundled in this repository (README.md's manual-copy list)
  from raw.githubusercontent.com, with a short timeout. If it
  succeeds, the newly downloaded themes are immediately cyclable; if
  the first request fails for any reason, it's read as "no network"
  and the question instead points at this repository's themes/
  directory and README.md for copying one in by hand. The base URL is
  a var rather than a const so tests can point it at an httptest
  server instead of the real network.

internal/ui/vocabtest's forge-vocabulary guard needed two new declared
exceptions for this: the repository URL and the "github-dark"/
"github-light" bundled theme names are not forge vocabulary, the same
way the About screen's own repository address isn't.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

---
name: feedback-wizard-one-question-at-a-time
description: Onboarding/setup wizards in this project should ask one question per screen with an explanation, not one dense multi-field form
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

For `dk setup` (`internal/ui/setup`), the user explicitly rejected a
single-screen form with every field visible at once (which I had built
first, following `internal/ui/components/CreationForm`'s pattern) in favor
of a step-by-step wizard: one question per screen, each with a short
explanation of what the choice means and its trade-offs, `enter` to answer
and move on, `esc` to go back one step.

**Why:** "au lieu d'avoir un seul formulaire a remplir j'aurais préféré
poser une question à la fois, en donnant du contexte et des explications
sur les différents choix pour vraiment assister l'utilisateur" — the goal
is to actually *assist* someone who may not know what e.g. "secret backend"
or "clone method" means, not just collect values quickly. This is the
opposite of the terse, all-at-once forms the rest of the app uses for quick
resource creation (`CreationForm` for groups/projects) — that pattern is
right for an experienced user doing a known, quick action; it is wrong for
a first-run onboarding flow.

**How to apply:** default to this step-by-step, explained style for any
future onboarding/wizard-shaped feature (as opposed to routine in-app
forms, which should keep following `CreationForm`'s single-screen
convention). See also [[feedback-setup-wizard-no-background]] — the same
package's styling also deliberately diverges from the rest of the app.

---
name: project-theme-remote-fetch
description: dk setup now fetches the repo's bundled themes over the network as a best-effort step — where the list lives and how it degrades
metadata:
  type: project
---

`internal/ui/setup/commands.go` added `fetchRemoteThemesCmd` (2026-09-13):
on reaching the theme question, the wizard makes a single best-effort
attempt to download the 12 themes bundled at this repo's root (`themes/*.json`,
previously only ever manually copied per README.md) from
`raw.githubusercontent.com/anthnel/devdesk/main/themes/`, with a short
(3s) per-file timeout, writing successes into `~/.devdesk/themes/`.

**Why:** before this, themes were purely local, hand-copied JSON files
with zero network involvement anywhere in the codebase (confirmed by
research — no prior mechanism existed). The user asked for the wizard to
offer importing them automatically when a network connection is available,
and to fall back to referencing the manual-copy docs otherwise, rather than
inventing a check-then-fetch two-step: a single attempt with a short
timeout is the whole detection mechanism (first failure = read as
"unreachable", no retry).

**How to apply:** the theme name list (`knownRemoteThemes` in
`commands.go`) is a **hardcoded duplicate** of `themes/*.json` at the repo
root — adding a new bundled theme file there must also add its name to
that list, or it won't be offered for download. `remoteThemeBaseURL` is a
package var (not a const) specifically so tests can redirect it to an
`httptest.Server`; don't hardcode the URL elsewhere. See
[[feedback-wizard-one-question-at-a-time]] for why this lives in a
step-by-step wizard rather than a form field.

1	// Package setup implements `dk setup`: a small standalone Bubble Tea program
2	// that walks a user through creating (or overwriting) a DevDesk context, one
3	// question at a time. It is not part of the app router — it runs before any
4	// context is loaded, so it builds a *config.Config from scratch and writes
5	// it with config.SaveContext, the same call the configuration view uses.
6	package setup
7	
8	import (
9		"log"
10		"strings"
11	
12		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
13		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
14		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
15	
16		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
17		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge"
18		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
19		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
20	)
21	
22	// Step indices, in the order the wizard asks them.
23	const (
24		stepFontCheck = iota
25		stepContextName
26		stepSecretBackend
27		stepContainerEngine
28		stepTheme
29		stepForgeType
30		stepForgeURL
31		stepForgeNamespace
32		stepForgeVisibility
33		stepForgeCloneMethod
34		stepForgeToken
35		stepCount
36	)
37	
38	// secretBackendOptions mirrors config.AppConfig.SecretBackend's closed set.
39	var secretBackendOptions = []string{"auto", "keyring", "git-credential"}
40	
41	// cloneMethodOptions mirrors config.ForgeConfig.CloneMethod's closed set.
42	var cloneMethodOptions = []string{"https", "ssh"}
43	
44	// fontCheckOptions is not a config value — nothing persists it — it only
45	// decides whether the remediation text is shown under the icon sample.
46	var fontCheckOptions = []string{"Looks correct", "Broken (boxes or question marks)"}
47	
48	// stage tracks what the wizard is doing, on top of which question is active.
49	type stage int
50	
51	const (
52		stageForm stage = iota
53		stageConfirmOverwrite
54		stageConfirmSetCurrent
55		stageDone
56	)
57	
58	// modalPurpose says what a Yes/No answer on the active confirm modal means —
59	// the wizard reuses one ConfirmModal for both of its confirmations rather
60	// than declaring two near-identical fields.
61	type modalPurpose int
62	
63	const (
64		modalNone modalPurpose = iota
65		modalOverwrite
66		modalSetCurrent
67	)
68	
69	// themeCheckState tracks the one-shot, best-effort attempt to fetch the
70	// bundled themes from the repository when the wizard reaches that question.
71	type themeCheckState int
72	
73	const (
74		themeCheckNotStarted themeCheckState = iota
75		themeCheckInFlight
76		themeCheckDone
77		themeCheckUnreachable
78	)
79	
80	// Model is the wizard: one question at a time (Rule 112's "form in the
81	// viewport" read literally per-step, rather than all fields on one screen —
82	// a deliberate choice for this screen alone, so every choice comes with the
83	// context to make it instead of a bare label).
84	type Model struct {
85		width, height int
86	
87		step         int
88		stage        stage
89		modalPurpose modalPurpose
90		confirmModal *confirmPrompt
91	
92		contextNameInput textinput.Model
93	
94		secretBackendIdx   int
95		containerEngineIdx int
96	
97		fontCheckIdx int
98	
99		themeOptions         []string
100		themeIdx             int
101		themeCheckState      themeCheckState
102		themeFetchAddedCount int
103	
104		forgeTypeIdx int
105		// forgeURLTouched stops the URL field from being overwritten once the user
106		// has typed into it, so switching Forge back and forth does not clobber a
107		// self-hosted URL they already entered.
108		forgeURLTouched     bool
109		forgeURLInput       textinput.Model
110		forgeNamespaceInput textinput.Model
111		visibilityValue     string
112		cloneMethodIdx      int
113		forgeTokenInput     textinput.Model
114	
115		// pending names the async step in flight, shown in the footer with a
116		// spinner (Rule 128); empty when nothing is running.
117		pending string
118		footer  components.FooterMessage
119		spinner spinner.Model
120	
121		savedPath             string
122		currentContextWarning string
123	}
124	
125	// New builds the wizard with every field at its default value.
126	func New() Model {
127		nameInput := textinput.New()
128		nameInput.Placeholder = "e.g. work, staging"
129		nameInput.CharLimit = 64
130		nameInput.Width = 40
131		styleTextInput(&nameInput)
132		nameInput.Focus()
133	
134		urlInput := textinput.New()
135		urlInput.CharLimit = 200
136		urlInput.Width = 50
137		styleTextInput(&urlInput)
138	
139		nsInput := textinput.New()
140		nsInput.Placeholder = "optional"
141		nsInput.CharLimit = 100
142		nsInput.Width = 40
143		styleTextInput(&nsInput)
144	
145		tokenInput := textinput.New()
146		tokenInput.Placeholder = "optional — can be set later via the auth view"
147		tokenInput.CharLimit = 200
148		tokenInput.Width = 50
149		tokenInput.EchoMode = textinput.EchoPassword
150		styleTextInput(&tokenInput)
151	
152		themes, err := theme.ListThemes()
153		if err != nil || len(themes) == 0 {
154			themes = []string{"default"}
155		}
156	
157		s := spinner.New()
158		s.Spinner = spinner.Dot
159		s.Style = spinnerStyle
160	
161		m := Model{
162			contextNameInput:    nameInput,
163			themeOptions:        themes,
164			forgeURLInput:       urlInput,
165			forgeNamespaceInput: nsInput,
166			visibilityValue:     "private",
167			forgeTokenInput:     tokenInput,
168			spinner:             s,
169		}
170		m.forgeURLInput.SetValue(forge.VocabularyFor(config.ForgeTypes()[m.forgeTypeIdx]).ExampleURL)
171		return m
172	}
173	
174	// Init starts the cursor blink, the only thing the wizard needs on launch.
175	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
176		return textinput.Blink
177	}
178	
179	// Update is the single Elm-architecture entry point (Rule 110): every field
180	// mutation happens here, never inside a Cmd.
181	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
182		switch msg := msg.(type) {
183		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
184			m.width = msg.Width
185			m.height = msg.Height
186			return m, nil
187	
188		case tea.KeyMsg:
189			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
190	
191		case spinner.TickMsg:
192			var cmd tea.Cmd
193			m.spinner, cmd = m.spinner.Update(msg)
194			return m, cmd
195	
196		case components.ConfirmModalYesMsg:
197			return m.handleConfirmYes()
198	
199		case components.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
200			return m.handleConfirmNo()
201	
202		case ContextExistsMsg:
203			return m.handleContextExists(msg)
204	
205		case RemoteThemesFetchedMsg:
206			return m.handleRemoteThemesFetched(msg)
207	
208		case TokenValidatedMsg:
209			return m.handleTokenValidated(msg)
210	
211		case ContextSavedMsg:
212			return m.handleContextSaved(msg)
213	
214		case CurrentContextSetMsg:
215			return m.handleCurrentContextSet(msg)
216		}
217	
218		if m.footer.Handle(msg) {
219			return m, nil
220		}
221		return m, nil
222	}
223	
224	func (m Model) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
225		if m.stage == stageConfirmOverwrite || m.stage == stageConfirmSetCurrent {
226			var cmd tea.Cmd
227			m.confirmModal, cmd = m.confirmModal.Update(msg)
228			return m, cmd
229		}
230		if m.stage == stageDone {
231			if msg.String() == "enter" || msg.String() == "esc" || msg.String() == "q" {
232				return m, tea.Quit
233			}
234			return m, nil
235		}
236	
237		switch msg.String() {
238		case "ctrl+c":
239			return m, tea.Quit
240		case "esc":
241			return m.stepBack()
242		case "left":
243			m.cycle(-1)
244			return m, nil
245		case "right":
246			m.cycle(1)
247			return m, nil
248		case "enter":
249			return m.advance()
250		}
251	
252		return m.updateFocusedInput(msg)
253	}
254	
255	// stepBack goes to the previous question, or quits from the first one —
256	// there is nothing before it to go back to (Rule 111: Esc cancels or returns
257	// to the parent level).
258	func (m Model) stepBack() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
259		if m.step == stepFontCheck {
260			return m, tea.Quit
261		}
262		m.step--
263		m.updateFocus()
264		return m, nil
265	}

---
name: feedback-setup-wizard-no-background
description: The dk setup wizard (internal/ui/setup) must not paint a background — deliberate exception to Rule 115
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 1aa17ae3-9a74-4371-83e6-959c689968de
  modified: 2026-09-13T09:21:14.303Z
---

`internal/ui/setup` (the `dk setup` context wizard) must NOT use any style
that calls `.Background(theme.ColorBackground)` — not the shared
`theme.TitleStyle`/`KeyStyle`/`HelpStyle`/`RenderButton`, not
`theme.Bg`/`EmptyLineBg`, not `theme.StyleTextInput`, and not
`components.FooterMessage.View()` (which background-fills and centers).
Local, no-background variants live in `internal/ui/setup/styles.go`
(`titleStyle`, `focusStyle`, `dimStyle`, `valueStyle`, `helpStyle`,
`errorStyle`/`warnStyle`/`infoStyle`, `spinnerStyle`, `styleTextInput`), same
colors, background dropped.

**Why:** the user reported "des problèmes de background" in the wizard and
asked explicitly to leave the background empty so it blends with whatever
terminal theme the user has: "je laisserais le background vide pour
s'intégrer avec le theme du terminal." The wizard is a standalone program
that runs before any context/theme is loaded, unlike every other view in
this app (which is governed by [[devdesk-tui-rules]] Rule 115: background is
mandatory everywhere, precisely so partial fills don't bleed). This is a
deliberate, scoped exception for this one package — not a project-wide
reversal of Rule 115.

**How to apply:** when touching `internal/ui/setup`, keep reusing the local
styles in `styles.go` instead of the shared `theme.*` background-forcing
ones. If a new themed helper is needed there, add a background-free local
variant rather than importing the themed one. Do not "fix" this back to
match Rule 115 without asking — it was a direct, explicit user request for
this specific screen.

content.content:
# GitHub OAuth Scopes Reference

## Core Repository Scopes

**repo**
Grants comprehensive access: "full access to public and private repositories including read and write access to code, commit statuses, repository invitations, collaborators, deployment statuses, and repository webhooks." Additionally enables management of organization resources and user-owned projects.

**public_repo**
Restricts permissions to public repositories only: "read/write access to code, commit statuses, repository projects, collaborators, and deployment statuses for public repositories and organizations." Required for starring public repositories.

**delete_repo**
Permits repository deletion: "access to delete adminable repositories."

## Organization Management Scopes

**read:org**
Provides view-only permissions: "read-only access to organization membership, organization projects, and team membership."

**write:org**
Enables modification capabilities: "read and write access to organization membership and organization projects."

**admin:org**
Grants complete control: "fully manage the organization and its teams, projects, and memberships."

## User Profile Scopes

**read:user**
Allows profile inspection: "access to read a user's profile data."

**user**
Expands access: "read/write access to profile info only." Note this scope implicitly includes `user:email` and `user:follow`.

## Additional Context

Scopes operate under principle of least privilege—they don't grant permissions beyond what the authorizing user already possesses. Users can modify granted scopes post-authorization, requiring applications to handle cases where reduced access is granted than initially requested.

content.content:
# Personal Access Token Scopes

## Complete List with Descriptions

**`api`**: "Grants complete read and write access to the API for the token's scope. Includes the container registry, the dependency proxy, and the package registry."

**`read_api`**: "Grants read access to the API for the token's scope. For a personal access token, includes the container registry and the package registry."

**`read_repository`**: "Grants read access (pull) to repositories for the token's scope: private projects for a personal access token."

**`write_repository`**: "Grants read and write access (pull and push) to repositories for the token's scope: private projects for a personal access token."

**`read_user`**: "Grants read-only access to the authenticated user's profile through the `/user` API endpoint, which includes username, public email, and full name."

## Key Clarifications

**Git HTTP Operations**: Yes, the `api` scope alone grants Git repository operations. The footnote explicitly states: "For a personal access token, `api` also grants complete read and write access to the registry and repository through Git-over-HTTP."

**Scope Relationship**: The `read_repository` and `write_repository` scopes represent *additional*, more restrictive alternatives—not requirements alongside `api`. They exist for granular control when you don't need full API access.

**API Coverage**: The `api` scope provides "complete read and write access to the API," which encompasses user profile data, but the documentation does not explicitly itemize whether group/project creation, deletion, or MR/issue operations are included.

9	// the application can promise, and no wording helps with them. Shape carries
10	// the second; this carries the first, and neither grows conditionals for the
11	// other.
12	//
13	// # Per forge, not neutral
14	//
15	// A GitLab user says *group*, a GitHub user says *repository*. "Namespace" is a
16	// third language nobody speaks, and it makes the application read as an
17	// abstraction layer rather than as a tool. So every word here is the one its
18	// forge's own documentation uses.
19	//
20	// The field names are neutral because the *code* has to be — a view cannot
21	// switch on which forge it is talking to — but nothing a user reads is.
22	//
23	// # No view writes a forge's name into a string
24	//
25	// That is the rule this type exists to make checkable, and
26	// TestNoViewNamesAForge (internal/ui/vocabtest) walks every string literal
27	// under internal/ui to enforce it. A command name is not covered: it is routing
28	// identity, the same for both forges, and lives in internal/command.

```go
func KeyringAvailable() bool {

}
```

```go
type Selection struct {
	Storage Storage
```

1	package setup

3	import (

11		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
12	)
13	
14	// bodyMaxWidth caps how wide an explanatory paragraph wraps, so a full-width
15	// terminal doesn't stretch a sentence edge to edge.
16	const bodyMaxWidth = 72
17	
18	// View renders the wizard: the current question, or whichever overlay is
19	// active on top of it (Rule 112 — a confirmation is a centered modal, never
20	// the viewport).
21	//
22	// Unlike every themed view, nothing here paints a background: the wizard
23	// runs standalone, before any theme is loaded, and is meant to sit on
24	// whatever terminal background the user already has (see styles.go).
25	func (m Model) View() string {
26		switch m.stage {
27		case stageConfirmOverwrite, stageConfirmSetCurrent:
28			return lipgloss.Place(m.width, m.height, lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center, m.confirmModal.View())
29		case stageDone:
30			return m.renderDone()
31		default:
32			return m.renderStep()
33		}
34	}
35	
36	// renderStep shows exactly one question — a title, the context to answer it
37	// with, and its control — rather than every field at once, so each choice
38	// comes with an explanation instead of a bare label (per the user's request:
39	// one question at a time, not a single long form).
40	func (m Model) renderStep() string {
41		var b strings.Builder
42	
43		b.WriteString(dimStyle.Render(fmt.Sprintf("Step %d of %d", m.step+1, stepCount)))
44		b.WriteString("\n\n")
45	
46		title, body, control := m.currentQuestion()
47	
48		b.WriteString(titleStyle.Render(title))
49		b.WriteString("\n\n")
50		if body != "" {
51			b.WriteString(bodyStyle(m.width).Render(body))
52			b.WriteString("\n\n")
53		}
54		b.WriteString(control)
55		b.WriteString("\n\n")
56	
57		b.WriteString(m.renderFooterLine())
58		b.WriteString("\n")
59		b.WriteString(helpStyle.Render(m.helpLine()))
60	
61		return b.String()
62	}
63	
64	// currentQuestion returns the active step's title, explanatory body, and
65	// rendered control. One function rather than one per step: every step needs
66	// the same three things, and the forge vocabulary the second half of the
67	// wizard reads from is resolved once here.
68	func (m Model) currentQuestion() (title, body, control string) {
69		v := forge.VocabularyFor(config.ForgeTypes()[m.forgeTypeIdx])
70	
71		switch m.step {
72		case stepFontCheck:
73			return m.fontCheckQuestion()
74	
75		case stepContextName:
76			return "Context name",
77				"A context is a complete, independent configuration — its own forge, " +
78					"secrets, and settings. Give this one a short name so you can tell it " +
79					"apart from others you create later (e.g. \"work\", \"client-a\"). " +
80					"Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only, or \"default\" for your " +
81					"main context.",
82				renderQuestionText("Name", m.contextNameInput.View())
83	
84		case stepSecretBackend:
85			return "Where to store secrets",
86				"DevDesk needs somewhere to keep your forge token. \"auto\" tries your OS " +
87					"keyring first, then git's credential helper, and falls back to " +
88					"memory-only — nothing survives past this session — if neither is " +
89					"available. Pick \"keyring\" or \"git-credential\" to require one " +
90					"specifically instead of silently falling back.",
91				renderQuestionCycle("Secret backend", secretBackendOptions[m.secretBackendIdx])
92	
93		case stepContainerEngine:
94			return "Container engine",
95				"DevDesk drives a container engine for image scanning and container " +
96					"management. \"auto\" prefers Docker when it's on PATH and falls back " +
97					"to Podman. Pick one explicitly if you have both installed and want " +
98					"DevDesk to always use the same one.",
99				renderQuestionCycle("Container engine", config.ContainerEngines()[m.containerEngineIdx])
100	
101		case stepTheme:
102			return m.themeQuestion()
103	
104		case stepForgeType:
105			return "Code hosting platform",
106				"Which platform hosts the repositories you work with? This decides the " +
107					"words DevDesk uses (Groups vs. Organizations, Merge Requests vs. Pull " +
108					"Requests) and which API it talks to.",
109				renderQuestionCycle("Forge", v.Name)
110	
111		case stepForgeURL:
112			return v.Name + " URL",
113				"The address of your " + v.Name + " instance. Leave the public default " +
114					"if that's what you use; change it for a self-hosted instance. Leave it " +
115					"blank to skip forge configuration for now — you can set it up later " +
116					"from the authentication view.",
117				renderQuestionText(v.Name+" URL", m.forgeURLInput.View())
118	
119		case stepForgeNamespace:
120			return "Default " + v.Namespace,
121				"The " + v.Namespace + " new repositories are created under by default, " +
122					"if you use DevDesk to create them. Leave it blank if you don't have " +
123					"one yet — you can always set it per repository.",
124				renderQuestionText("Default "+v.Namespace, m.forgeNamespaceInput.View())
125	
126		case stepForgeVisibility:
127			return "Default visibility",
128				visibilityBody(v, m.visibilityOptions()),
129				renderQuestionCycle("Visibility", m.visibilityValue)
130	
131		case stepForgeCloneMethod:
132			return "Clone method",
133				"How DevDesk clones your repositories. \"https\" works everywhere and " +
134					"may prompt for your token; \"ssh\" uses your configured SSH key and " +
135					"needs no further authentication for git operations.",
136				renderQuestionCycle("Clone method", cloneMethodOptions[m.cloneMethodIdx])
137	
138		case stepForgeToken:
139			return v.TokenLabel,
140				v.TokenHelp + " It is checked against " + v.Name + " before being saved. " +
141					"Leave it blank to configure this later from the authentication view — " +

148	// fontCheckQuestion is the wizard's first screen: a sample of the Nerd Font
149	// glyphs every other screen (and the rest of the app) renders with, so a
150	// broken font is caught before the user spends the rest of setup looking at

152	// saved — cycling it only changes whether the remediation text below is
153	// shown.
154	func (m Model) fontCheckQuestion() (title, body, control string) {
155		sample := strings.Join([]string{
156			theme.IconCircleSmall, theme.IconChevronRight, theme.IconSelect,
157			theme.IconOK, theme.IconWarning, theme.IconError,
158		}, "  ")
159	
160		body = "DevDesk uses a Nerd Font for its icons, throughout this wizard and the " +
161			"rest of the application. The line below should show a handful of small, " +
162			"distinct glyphs — a dot, an arrow, a checkmark — not boxes, question " +
163			"marks, or blank squares."
164		if m.fontCheckIdx == 1 {
165			body += "\n\nInstall a Nerd Font from https://www.nerdfonts.com/font-downloads " +
166				"and set it as your terminal's font, then restart the terminal. This does " +
167				"not block setup — you can continue now and fix it later."
168		}
169	
170		control = valueStyle.Render(sample) + "\n\n" +
171			renderQuestionCycle("Icons render correctly?", fontCheckOptions[m.fontCheckIdx])
172		return "Terminal font check", body, control
173	}

175	// themeQuestion reflects the one-shot background fetch's state: in flight,
176	// unreachable (with a pointer to the manual-copy docs), or done.
177	func (m Model) themeQuestion() (title, body, control string) {
178		body = "Pick the color theme DevDesk renders with."
179		switch m.themeCheckState {
180		case themeCheckUnreachable:
181			body += " Only the built-in theme is available right now — no network " +
182				"reachable to fetch more. Browse the rest at " +
183				"https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/tree/main/themes and copy one into " +
184				"~/.devdesk/themes/ by hand; see README.md for the exact steps."
185		case themeCheckDone:

194	// visibilityBody explains the current forge's visibility options — "internal"
195	// only exists for the ones that have one.
196	func visibilityBody(v forge.Vocabulary, opts []string) string {
197		body := "How visible should repositories DevDesk creates be by default? " +
198			"\"private\" — only you and people you explicitly grant access."
199		for _, o := range opts {
200			if o == "internal" {
201				body += " \"internal\" — visible to every authenticated user of this " + v.Name + " instance."
202			}
203		}

209		var b strings.Builder
210	
211		b.WriteString(titleStyle.Render("Context ready"))
212		b.WriteString("\n\n")
213		b.WriteString("Wrote " + m.savedPath)
214		b.WriteString("\n")

216			b.WriteString(errorStyle.Render(m.currentContextWarning))
217			b.WriteString("\n")
218		}
219		b.WriteString("\n")

224		return b.String()

227	// renderFooterLine reads components.FooterMessage's state directly instead of
228	// calling its View — that method paints a full-width, background-filled,
229	// centered line (Rule 128), which is exactly what this screen opts out of.
230	func (m Model) renderFooterLine() string {
231		if m.footer.IsSet() {
232			return footerLevelStyle(m.footer.Level()).Render(m.footer.Text())
233		}
234		if m.pending != "" {
235			return m.spinner.View() + " " + dimStyle.Render(m.pending)
236		}
237		return ""

240	// helpLine lists this step's keys — only the ones that apply, since a
241	// cycle key on a text question would be a lie about what it does.
242	func (m Model) helpLine() string {
243		help := "  [enter] continue"
244		if isCycleStep(m.step) {
245			help += "  [←→] change"
246		}
247		if m.step == stepFontCheck {

255	func isCycleStep(step int) bool {
256		switch step {
257		case stepFontCheck, stepSecretBackend, stepContainerEngine, stepTheme,

259			return true
260		}

264	// bodyStyle wraps an explanatory paragraph to a readable width regardless of
265	// how wide the terminal is.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix: detect unreachable secret backend and container engine as early as possible

This is the bug a user hit directly: they picked "keyring", entered a
GitLab token, the wizard reported success, and the real app later
showed them logged out — "Nothing is saved — Secret Service is
configured but not reachable." credentials.Select already knew this at
selection time (Selection.Persists()/Detail), but nothing in the
wizard ever asked it before or after saving the token.

Two fixes:

- The secret backend question now runs credentials.Select for real,
  live, every time the answer changes (and on first arriving at the
  step) and shows exactly what it would say in the auth view —
  "Secrets are stored in the Secret Service" or the same "not
  reachable" warning — right there, before a token is even typed.

- The token step's actual save is checked the same way: if
  Authenticate's own write fails, or if Select had already resolved to
  memory-only storage, that warning now survives to the final "Context
  ready" screen instead of being silently discarded once the token
  itself validated successfully.

The container engine question gets the analogous fix for "podman must
be up, same for docker": it now resolves the candidate engine
(internal/engine.Resolve) and asks whether its daemon actually answers
(internal/docker.FetchCapacity), not just whether the binary is on
PATH — which is all the dashboard's own tool detection checks today.

internal/ui/setup/commands.go's cycle() now returns a tea.Cmd, since
two of its questions re-run a live check on every change; the spinner
that shows while a check is running needed its tick loop actually
started, which nothing here did before (a latent bug: the spinner
model existed but nothing ever kicked off spinner.Tick).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

---
name: feedback-wizard-detect-early
description: dk setup must live-check anything it lets the user pick, not just accept the choice and let it fail silently later
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

The user hit a real bug: picked "keyring" as secret backend in `dk setup`,
entered a GitLab token, the wizard said everything succeeded, then the real
app showed them logged out — the auth view's own text: "Nothing is saved —
Secret Service is configured but not reachable. You will have to
authenticate again next launch." `credentials.Select` already knew this at
selection time (`Selection.Persists()`/`Selection.Detail`); nothing in the
wizard had ever asked it.

**Why:** "il faudrait que le wizard fasse les tests et affichent ces infos
car je pensais que tout s'était bien passé" — a wizard that lets you pick
something and only reports failure indirectly, elsewhere, after the fact,
is worse than no check at all: it actively creates false confidence. The
user generalized this immediately to the container engine question too:
"si je choisi podman, il faut que podman soit up, idem pour docker, donc le
wizard doit détecter au plus tôt ce qui ne va pas" — detect as early as
possible, for any choice that has a real/not-real distinction, not just the
one they happened to hit.

**How to apply:** for `internal/ui/setup`, and for any future wizard-shaped
feature ([[feedback-wizard-one-question-at-a-time]]), a question whose
answer has a live-reachable/not-reachable dimension must:
1. Run the real check (reusing the app's own existing detection —
   `credentials.Select`, `internal/engine.Resolve` +
   `internal/docker.FetchCapacity` — never a wizard-local guess) live,
   every time the answer changes, not just once.
2. Surface the exact same wording the rest of the app already uses for that
   state (`Selection.Detail`), so there is one sentence per situation, not a
   second one invented for the wizard.
3. Re-verify at the point of actual commitment too (saving the token), not
   only at the point of selection — the two can diverge, and the final
   screen must never claim success while quietly swallowing a warning
   (`components.FooterMessage`-style transient toasts are wrong for this —
   the warning must survive to the persistent Done screen, not expire after
   3 seconds).
See [[project-theme-remote-fetch]] for the existing "check live, degrade
with an explanation" pattern this follows (the theme fetch), and
`internal/ui/setup/commands.go`'s `checkSecretBackendCmd`/
`checkContainerEngineCmd` for the concrete implementation.

### 3.73 `table_line_selected` — nouvelle clé, et `severity_low` recoloré sur le ton des « 0 »

Demande directe, faisant suite à §3.72 : sortir le fond de la sélection
« normale » de sa dépendance à `ColorSeverityLow` pour lui donner sa **propre**
clé de thème, puis changer la couleur de `severity_low` elle-même pour
reprendre le ton déjà utilisé par les compteurs à `0` de l'écran `:sec`
(`inventory_table.go`, `countColumn` — `theme.DimStyle`, qui aliase
`ColorDim`).

**Nouvelle clé : `ColorTableLineSelected` / `table_line_selected`.**
`DefaultTableStyles()`, et les deux branches `selected` de `render.go`
(`cellStyle`, `runStyle`) qui peignent le fond de la sélection « normale »
cellule par cellule (§3.72), lisent maintenant cette clé plutôt que
`ColorSeverityLow` directement. Sa valeur par défaut est `#313244` —
exactement l'ancienne valeur par défaut de `severity_low` — pour que ce
changement seul ne change rien à l'écran. `m.preserveColumnColors`
(`datatable.go`) compare désormais le fond résolu à `ColorTableLineSelected`
plutôt qu'à `ColorSeverityLow` pour détecter la sélection « normale ».

**`severity_low` prend le ton de `ColorDim`.** Sa valeur par défaut passe de
`#313244` à `#585b70` — celle de `color_dim`. `SeverityTextStyle("LOW")` et
`TableStylesForSeverity("LOW")` en héritent automatiquement puisqu'ils lisent
`ColorSeverityLow` en direct : le texte d'une sévérité LOW, et le fond de la
ligne sélectionnée d'une trouvaille LOW, prennent tous deux ce gris plutôt que
l'ancien mauve-nuit à peine plus clair que le fond de l'application. Le
fallback de `ColorSeverityLow` dans `ApplyTheme` passe pareillement de
`ColorCmdLineBg` à `ColorDim`, pour qu'un thème qui ne fixe pas
`severity_low` obtienne la nouvelle intention plutôt que l'ancienne
coïncidence.

**Conséquence sur les jauges de charge (§3.71).** `theme.GaugeTrackStyle()`
continue d'aliaser `ColorSeverityLow` pour le rail — rien n'y change dans le
code — mais la couleur elle-même devient littéralement celle de `ColorDim`,
ce que le commentaire de `gauge.go` affirmait *ne pas* être vrai
(« a severity colour says [low] and a grey does not ») ; le commentaire est
corrigé en conséquence plutôt que le code, l'affirmation étant devenue fausse
par construction. La distinction reste réelle par le **nom** de la clé (un
thème peut toujours séparer `severity_low` de `color_dim`), simplement plus
par sa valeur par défaut.

**Sur une ligne sélectionnée, le rail redevient visible.** §3.72 puis la
correction du 2026-09-09 (gauge-mem) faisaient coïncider, par construction,
l'avant-plan du rail (`ColorSeverityLow`) et le fond de la sélection — ce qui
rendait le rail invisible sous le curseur, un accident de deux clés qui
pointaient alors la même valeur. Les deux clés étant maintenant distinctes et
de valeurs différentes (`#585b70` contre `#313244`), le rail redevient un
gris visible sur le fond de sélection, cohérent avec son apparence sur une
ligne non sélectionnée plutôt qu'un cas particulier invisible.

**Les douze thèmes fournis (`themes/`) reçoivent le même traitement.**
`DefaultTheme()` n'est que le thème intégré au binaire ; les fichiers de
`themes/` (copiés par l'utilisateur dans `~/.devdesk/themes/`, README
§"Themes") sont indépendants et n'auraient sinon jamais gagné
`table_line_selected` ni le recolorage. Pour chacun : `table_line_selected`
prend l'ancienne valeur de `severity_low` de **ce même fichier** (jamais celle
du thème par défaut), pour que la sélection ne bouge pas ; `severity_low`
prend ensuite la valeur de `color_dim` de ce même fichier. Un thème comme
`nord` ou `solarized-light`, dont la palette n'a rien à voir avec Catppuccin,
garde donc sa propre teinte de gris plutôt que d'hériter de `#585b70`.
Deux fichiers (`one-dark.json`, `tokyo-night.json`) utilisaient une
indentation à 4 espaces plutôt que 2 ; elle est préservée par fichier plutôt
qu'uniformisée, pour ne pas gonfler la diff avec un reformatage sans rapport.

---

## 4. Existing plans

Detailed plans live in `.claude/plans/`. One is outstanding:

- [`platform_compatibility_improvements.md`](../.claude/plans/platform_compatibility_improvements.md)
  — Docker-layer platform portability. Referenced from the old `todo.md`.

Plans for shipped work are removed from `.claude/plans/` once their feature
lands and the corresponding §3.x entry above is marked **done** — the backlog
entry is the lasting record, not the plan file.

12168	CLI. `dockerConfigPath()` (`internal/docker/registry.go:45`) code le chemin en
12169	dur, `readDockerConfig` (`registry.go:54`) le désérialise, et
12170	`removeFromDockerConfig` fait un `os.WriteFile` dessus (`registry.go:157`) —

12241	binaire, et remplacer une dépendance légère par une lourde des deux côtés.
12242	
12243	#### Ce qui a été fait — 2026-09-12
12244	
12245	`internal/engine` porte une `Shape` par moteur : le binaire, le préfixe des
12246	helpers d'identifiants, le fichier d'auth, le socket, et les gabarits. C'est un
12247	paquet à part et pas un champ de `internal/docker`, parce que `internal/scan` a
12248	besoin de la même réponse et n'importe pas `internal/docker` — l'arrangement de
12249	`internal/forge` lu un cran plus bas.
12250	
12251	Les quatre frictions, dans l'ordre où elles sont listées plus haut :
12252	
12253	1. **Le fichier d'auth** passe par `Shape.AuthPath()` : `~/.docker/config.json`
12254	   sous docker, `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/containers/auth.json` puis
12255	   `~/.config/containers/auth.json` sous podman. Le JSON est le même des deux
12256	   côtés, donc tous les lecteurs et la réécriture en 0600 sont inchangés.
12257	2. **Le socket** vient de la shape et passe par `ToolSpec.HostSocket`. Le côté
12258	   conteneur reste `/var/run/docker.sock` — c'est là que trivy regarde — seul le
12259	   côté hôte bouge. Un socket absent ne produit **aucun** montage : `S` sur une
12260	   image est grisé avec sa raison (« podman socket not found — run `podman
12261	   system service` … »), ce qui est la Rule 130 appliquée à ce qu'on sait avant
12262	   la frappe. Le scan de **répertoire** reste disponible, il ne monte rien.
12263	3. **`internal/scan`** : les six sites lisent `engine.Current()`, et
12264	   `ToolSourceDocker` est devenu `ToolSourceContainer`. Vérifié avant de le
12265	   faire : cette valeur n'est **pas** sérialisée, et la config dit déjà la même
12266	   chose sans nommer de moteur (`ToolSourceImage = "image"`). Pas de migration.
12267	4. **Le shell, le pager et le dashboard** lisent la shape.
12268	
12269	**Le réglage** est `app.container_engine`, un champ cyclé dans le groupe
12270	*External commands*, réglé au blur comme la forge — cycler
12271	auto → docker → podman le résoudrait sinon trois fois, y compris au retour à la
12272	valeur de départ. `ConfigSavedMsg.EngineChanged` prévient le routeur : rebâtir
12273	les vues ne suffit pas, elles le seraient contre le moteur encore résolu. Une

**Les onze sorties parsées ne sont toujours pas mesurées.** Il n'y a pas de
podman sur la machine où ceci a été écrit (vérifié : `podman: command not
found`). Les deux jeux de gabarits sont donc **identiques**, et
`TestTheTwoTemplateSetsAreStillUnmeasured` échoue le jour où ils cessent de
l'être — pour que la divergence soit enregistrée volontairement plutôt que
découverte par une ligne fausse. L'indirection ne prétend pas résoudre le
problème : elle fait que la correction sera d'une ligne dans
`shapes["podman"].Templates` au lieu d'un refactor. La liste exacte à passer
contre un vrai podman est dans le doc du paquet et dans le plan.

**`system df -v` est désactivé sous podman** (`Shape.ParsesSystemDFVerbose`).
C'est la douzième sortie, et la seule sans gabarit : un tableau à colonnes
fixes découpé aux offsets pris sur sa ligne d'en-tête. `UniqueSize` et
`Containers` restent à zéro, ce que la table rend en `-` : une absence se lit
comme une absence, une valeur découpée dans la mauvaise colonne non.

**Le paquet s'appelle toujours `internal/docker`.** Le renommer toucherait 40
fichiers pour un gain de vocabulaire et brouillerait la revue du vrai
changement. À reprendre si le besoin se confirme.

**Une `Shape` ne porte aucun chemin résolu.** Les stocker a été essayé et
annulé : la shape est construite à l'initialisation du paquet, donc un `$HOME`
lu là est figé avant que quoi que ce soit d'autre tourne — attrapé par les tests
d'`oci_resources`, qui déplacent `HOME` dans leur `TestMain`. Le socket est pire
encore, puisque son existence *est* toute la question et que `podman system
service` peut démarrer ou s'arrêter pendant que l'application tourne.

**Le pager de logs ne met pas le binaire entre guillemets.**
`TestThePagerCommandCarriesNoQuote` l'interdit — `exec.Command` échappe le
guillemet et `cmd.exe` ne le comprend pas. Le coût, énoncé plutôt que
découvert : un chemin de moteur contenant une espace casse `V`, et seulement
là.
